lessons.title: Exercise 1.1 — Reading and Writing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Groups of Three

To read a big number, split it into groups of three digits from the right. The groups are ones, thousands, millions and billions.

Reading a Number

Read each group like a small number, then say the group name. For example, 171,283,680 is read as one hundred seventy one million, two hundred eighty three thousand, six hundred eighty.

Writing in Figures

  • One million two thousand six hundred has parts 1,000,000, 2,000 and 600, which together make 1,002,600.
  • One billion is written as 1,000,000,000.
  • Empty groups are filled with zeros.

mcqs.q: How is 45,672 written in words?
options: Forty five thousand six hundred twenty seven
Forty five thousand six hundred seventy two
Four hundred fifty six thousand seventy two
Forty five thousand six hundred seven
mcqs.why: Split 45,672 into groups: 45 thousand and 672. So 45,000 + 672 = 45,672, read as forty five thousand six hundred seventy two.

mcqs.q: How is 2,670,273 written in words?
options: Two million six hundred seven thousand two hundred seventy three
Two hundred sixty seven million two hundred seventy three
Two million six hundred seventy thousand two hundred seventy three
Twenty six million seventy thousand two hundred seventy three
mcqs.why: The groups are 2 million, 670 thousand and 273 ones. Reading them in order gives two million six hundred seventy thousand two hundred seventy three.

mcqs.q: Write in figures: One million two thousand six hundred.
mcqs.why: Put the parts together group by group: the parts 1,000,000, 2,000 and 600 together make 1,002,600. The thousands group is 002, so zeros must be written there.

mcqs.q: Write in figures: Nine million ninety nine thousand seventy seven.
mcqs.why: Put the parts together group by group: the parts 9,000,000, 99,000 and 77 together make 9,099,077. The ones group is 077, so a zero is written before 77.

mcqs.q: How is 100,000,000 written in words?
mcqs.why: The number 100,000,000 has groups 100 million, 000 thousand and 000 ones, so it is read simply as one hundred million.

mcqs.q: Write in figures: Fifty eight million eight hundred sixty two thousand forty five.
mcqs.why: Put the parts together group by group: the parts 58,000,000, 862,000 and 45 together make 58,862,045. The ones group is 045, so a zero comes before 45.

mcqs.q: In 171,283,680, which group shows the thousands?
mcqs.why: Grouping from the right gives 171 million, 283 thousand and 680 ones, so the middle group 283 is the thousands group of the number.

mcqs.q: How is one billion written in figures?
mcqs.why: One billion is one thousand million. It has ten digits and is written as 1,000,000,000, with groups 1 billion and all other groups zero.

mcqs.q: How is 34,296,127 written in words?
options: Thirty four million two hundred ninety six thousand one hundred twenty six
Thirty four million two hundred sixty nine thousand one hundred twenty seven
Three hundred forty two million ninety six thousand one hundred twenty seven
Thirty four million two hundred ninety six thousand one hundred twenty seven
mcqs.why: The groups are 34 million, 296 thousand and 127 ones. Reading them in order gives thirty four million two hundred ninety six thousand one hundred twenty seven.

mcqs.q: How is 66,655,522 written in words?
options: Sixty six million six hundred fifty five thousand five hundred twenty two
Sixty six million six hundred fifty five thousand five hundred twenty five
Six hundred sixty six million five hundred fifty two thousand twenty two
Sixty six million six hundred fifty thousand five hundred twenty two
mcqs.why: The groups are 66 million, 655 thousand and 522 ones, read as sixty six million six hundred fifty five thousand five hundred twenty two.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.2 — Addition
lessons.notes_html:
Column Addition

Write the numbers in columns so that ones are under ones, tens under tens, and so on. Add from the right side first.

Carrying Over

  • If a column total is 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the rest to the next column.
  • Example: 713,492 + 268,310 = 981,802.
  • For word problems, add all the amounts together, for example a total bill.

mcqs.why: Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 713,492 + 268,310 = 981,802. Check the ones column: 2 + 0 = 2, which matches the last digit.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 4,318,114 + 313,934 = 4,632,048. The thousands part grows because of a carry from the hundreds column.

mcqs.q: Operation charges were Rs. 350,000, room charges Rs. 1,200 and medicine charges Rs. 125,500. What was the total hospital bill?
mcqs.why: Add step by step: 350,000 + 1,200 = 351,200, and then 351,200 + 125,500 = 476,700. So the total bill was Rs. 476,700.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 680,563 + 563,168 = 1,243,731. The answer passes one million because the hundred-thousands column carries over.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 8,193,860 + 429,177 = 8,623,037. Check the ones column: 0 + 7 = 7, matching the last digit 7.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 5,491,869 + 605,304 = 6,097,173. Check the ones column: 9 + 4 = 13, so write 3 and carry 1.

mcqs.q: An addition sum has first number 536,2_4, second number 353,422 and total 889,636. What is the missing tens digit of the first number?
mcqs.why: Work in the tens column: the ones give 4 + 2 = 6 with no carry, so in the tens column the missing digit plus 2 must give 3, which makes the missing digit 1. The full sum 536,214 + 353,422 = 889,636 confirms it.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 34,653,635 + 2,660,477 = 37,314,112. Check the ones column: 5 + 7 = 12, so write 2 and carry 1.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 438,394,568 + 351,056,939 = 789,451,507. The millions group becomes 789 after all the carries are included.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 3,541,371 + 232,164 = 3,773,535. Check the ones column: 1 + 4 = 5, matching the last digit 5.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.3 — Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Column Subtraction

Write the bigger number on top and subtract in columns from the right. The answer is called the difference.

Borrowing

  • If the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit, borrow 1 from the column on the left.
  • Example: 2,863,132 - 164,350 = 2,698,782.
  • For how many more questions, subtract the smaller amount from the bigger amount.

mcqs.why: Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where the top digit is smaller: 2,863,132 - 164,350 = 2,698,782. Check by adding back: the difference plus 164,350 gives the first number.

mcqs.q: Subtract 214,379 from 600,500.
mcqs.why: Subtract the smaller number from the bigger one, borrowing across the zeros: 600,500 - 214,379 = 386,121. The zeros in 600,500 make borrowing the tricky part here.

mcqs.q: Pakistan imported 107,857 kg dry grapes in 2014 and 154,792 kg in 2015. How many more kg were imported in 2015?
mcqs.why: Subtract the smaller quantity from the larger one: 154,792 - 107,857 = 46,935. So 46,935 kg more dry grapes were imported in 2015 than in 2014.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 5,634,153 - 393,844 = 5,240,309. Check the ones column: 13 - 4 = 9 after borrowing, matching the last digit.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 4,194,312 - 994,208 = 3,200,104. Check the ones column: 12 - 8 = 4 after borrowing, matching the last digit.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 50,862,131 - 944,029 = 49,918,102. The millions part drops below 50 because of the borrowing chain.

mcqs.q: In 873,246 - 431,12_ = 442,123, what is the missing ones digit of the lower number?
mcqs.why: Find the lower number first: 873,246 - 442,123 = 431,123. So the complete subtraction is 873,246 - 431,123 = 442,123, and the missing ones digit is 3.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 656,148,154 - 134,258,369 = 521,889,785. Check the ones column: 14 - 9 = 5 after borrowing.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 89,086,371 - 35,180,962 = 53,905,409. Check the ones column: 11 - 2 = 9 after borrowing, matching the last digit.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 43,547,967 - 5,396,138 = 38,151,829. Check the ones column: 17 - 8 = 9 after borrowing, matching the last digit.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.4 — Multiplication
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplying by 10, 100 and 1,000

For times 10 put one zero at the end, for times 100 put two zeros, and for times 1,000 put three zeros. Example: 4,136 x 10 = 41,360.

Bigger Multiplications

  • Multiply by the ones, then by the tens, then by the hundreds.
  • Add the partial products at the end.
  • Example: 25,839 x 3 = 77,517 and 25,839 x 30 = 775,170, and 77,517 + 775,170 = 852,687.

mcqs.why: Multiplying by 10 puts one zero at the end of the number: 4,136 x 10 = 41,360. The digits stay the same and only shift one place to the left.
Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end of the number: 15,347 x 100 = 1,534,700. Count the zeros in 100 and add the same number of zeros.
Multiplying by 1,000 puts three zeros at the end of the number: 41,357 x 1,000 = 41,357,000. Count the zeros in 1,000 and add the same number of zeros.
First multiply by 5 and then by 10: 1,942 x 5 = 9,710, and then 9,710 x 10 = 97,100. So 1,942 x 50 = 97,100.
Use partial products: 25,839 x 3 = 77,517 and 25,839 x 30 = 775,170. Adding them gives 77,517 + 775,170 = 852,687.

mcqs.q: The school library ordered 45 books at Rs. 325 each. What is the total cost?
mcqs.why: Multiply the cost of one book by the number of books: 325 x 40 = 13,000 and 325 x 5 = 1,625, and then 13,000 + 1,625 = 14,625 rupees.
Multiplying by 100 puts two zeros at the end of the number: 155,430 x 100 = 15,543,000. The number already ends in a zero, and two more zeros are added.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.5 — Division
lessons.notes_html:
Long Division

Division shares a number into equal parts. The answer is the quotient, and what is left over is the remainder.

Dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000

  • For 10, the last 1 digit is the remainder.
  • For 100, the last 2 digits are the remainder.
  • For 1,000, the last 3 digits are the remainder.
  • Example: 61,500 / 500 = 123, because 123 x 500 = 61,500.

mcqs.why: By long division, 295,845 / 33 = 8,965 with nothing left over. Check by multiplying back: 33 x 8,965 = 295,845, so the quotient is correct.

mcqs.q: Find the quotient and remainder: 5,678 / 10 = ?
mcqs.why: When dividing by 10, the last digit is the remainder and the rest of the number is the quotient. So dividing 5,678 by 10 gives quotient 567 and remainder 8, since 567 x 10 = 5,670 and 5,670 + 8 = 5,678.

mcqs.q: Mr. Anwar cooks 61,500 naans in 500 days, the same number each day. How many naans does he cook daily?
mcqs.why: Divide the total by the days: 61,500 / 500 = 123. Cancel two zeros from both numbers to get 615 / 5 = 123, and check: 123 x 500 = 61,500.
By long division the quotient is 6,399. Check: 89 x 6,399 = 569,511, and then 569,511 + 40 = 569,551, so the remainder is 40.

mcqs.q: Find the quotient and remainder: 473,405 / 100 = ?
mcqs.why: When dividing by 100, the last two digits form the remainder. The last two digits are 05, so dividing 473,405 by 100 gives quotient 4,734 and remainder 5.

mcqs.q: Find the quotient and remainder: 8,256,879 / 1,000 = ?
mcqs.why: When dividing by 1,000, the last three digits form the remainder. The last three digits are 879, so dividing 8,256,879 by 1,000 gives quotient 8,256 and remainder 879.
Cancel one zero from both numbers and divide 57,648 / 6 = 9,608. Check by multiplying back: 9,608 x 60 = 576,480, so the quotient is correct.
By long division the quotient is 1,385. Check: 321 x 1,385 = 444,585, and then 444,585 + 186 = 444,771, so the remainder is 186.
Cancel one zero from both numbers and divide 26,976 / 48 = 562. Check by multiplying back: 562 x 480 = 269,760, so the quotient is correct.
By long division, 466,896 / 822 = 568 with nothing left over. Check by multiplying back: 568 x 822 = 466,896, so the quotient is correct.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.6 — Real Life Problems (Mixed Operations)
lessons.notes_html:
Choosing the Operation

Read the problem carefully and decide what to do: altogether usually means add, left or borrowed usually means subtract, each or per with equal sharing means divide, and the same amount many times means multiply.

Examples

  • Altogether: 145,320 + 54,304 = 199,624.
  • Change back: 5,000 - 2,300 = 2,700.
  • Equal sharing: 531,675 / 45 = 11,815.

mcqs.q: Fouzia had 145,320 rupees. Her father gave her 54,304 rupees more. How many rupees did she have altogether?
mcqs.why: Altogether means add the two amounts: 145,320 + 54,304 = 199,624. So Fouzia had 199,624 rupees in total after her father gave her the money.

mcqs.q: Sobia gave a 5,000 rupee note for a doll worth Rs. 2,300. How much money did she get back?
mcqs.why: The money received back is found by subtracting the price from the note: 5,000 - 2,300 = 2,700. So Sobia received Rs. 2,700 back from the shopkeeper.

mcqs.q: A factory produced 235,806 floor tiles in one day. How many tiles will it produce in 32 days?
mcqs.why: Multiply the one-day production by 32: 235,806 x 30 = 7,074,180 and 235,806 x 2 = 471,612, and then 7,074,180 + 471,612 = 7,545,792 tiles.

mcqs.q: The government spent Rs. 5,380,100 on gas supply in one town. How much will it spend on 25 such towns?
mcqs.why: Multiply the cost for one town by 25: 5,380,100 x 25 = 134,502,500. A quick way is 5,380,100 x 100 = 538,010,000, and one fourth of that is the answer.

mcqs.q: One container holds 9,475 litres of milk. How many litres will 354 such containers hold?
mcqs.why: Multiply using partial products: 9,475 x 300 = 2,842,500 and 9,475 x 54 = 511,650, and then 2,842,500 + 511,650 = 3,354,150 litres of milk.

mcqs.q: One roll contains 45 metres of cloth. How many rolls are needed to pack 531,675 metres of cloth?
mcqs.why: Divide the total cloth by the length in one roll: 531,675 / 45 = 11,815. Check by multiplying back: 11,815 x 45 = 531,675, so 11,815 rolls are needed.

mcqs.q: A company needed Rs. 52,890,500 for land. It had Rs. 50,456,128 and borrowed the rest. How much did it borrow?
mcqs.why: The borrowed amount is the difference between the price and the money the company already had: 52,890,500 - 50,456,128 = 2,434,372 rupees borrowed from the bank.

mcqs.q: 225 students contributed equally a total of Rs. 23,650 for flood relief. How much did each student contribute in whole rupees, and how much was left over?
mcqs.why: Divide the total by the number of students: 225 x 105 = 23,625, and then 23,625 + 25 = 23,650. So each student gave Rs. 105 and Rs. 25 were left over.

mcqs.q: A factory produced 235,806 floor tiles in one day. How many tiles will it produce in 30 days?
mcqs.why: Multiply the one-day production by 30: 235,806 x 30 = 7,074,180. First do 235,806 x 3 = 707,418, then put one zero at the end for times 30.

mcqs.q: After receiving money from her father, Fouzia had 199,624 rupees. She had 145,320 rupees at the start. How much did her father give her?
mcqs.why: Subtract the starting amount from the final amount: 199,624 - 145,320 = 54,304. So her father gave her 54,304 rupees, which matches the original problem.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.7 — BODMAS Rule
lessons.notes_html:
The BODMAS Order

BODMAS tells us the order of doing operations: Brackets first, then of (which means multiply), then Divide, then Multiply, then Add, and at last Subtract.

Worked Example

  • Brackets: 213 - 123 = 90 and 64 / 8 = 8.
  • Multiply: 60 x 5 = 300.
  • Add and subtract: 90 + 300 = 390, and then 390 - 8 = 382.
  • Division and multiplication have equal rank, so do them from left to right.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: (9 - 8) x 18 = ?
mcqs.why: Do the bracket first: 9 - 8 = 1. Then multiply: 1 x 18 = 18. Brackets always come before multiplication in the BODMAS order.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 16 / 2 + 5 x 4 - 2 = ?
mcqs.why: Divide and multiply before adding and subtracting: 16 / 2 = 8 and 5 x 4 = 20. Then work left to right: 8 + 20 = 28, and 28 - 2 = 26.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 50 x 5 + (15 + 23) = ?
mcqs.why: Do the bracket first: 15 + 23 = 38. Then multiply: 50 x 5 = 250. At last add: 250 + 38 = 288, following the BODMAS order.

mcqs.q: Salman solved (213 - 123) + 60 x 5 - (64 / 8). What is the correct answer?
mcqs.why: Brackets first: 213 - 123 = 90 and 64 / 8 = 8. Then multiply: 60 x 5 = 300. Then add and subtract: 90 + 300 = 390, and 390 - 8 = 382.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 4 of 195 / 13 - 54 = ?
mcqs.why: The word of means multiply, and it comes before division: 4 x 195 = 780. Then divide: 780 / 13 = 60. At last subtract: 60 - 54 = 6.

mcqs.q: Which brackets make the statement 6 x 2 + 8 / 4 give the answer 15?
mcqs.why: Check the bracketed form step by step: the bracket gives 2 + 8 = 10, then 6 x 10 = 60, and then 60 / 4 = 15. Without brackets the left side gives only 14, so the brackets are needed.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: (5 x 9) / 15 = ?
mcqs.why: Do the bracket first: 5 x 9 = 45. Then divide: 45 / 15 = 3. Brackets come first in the BODMAS order, before division.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 32 x 21 - 42 / 7 = ?
mcqs.why: Multiply and divide before subtracting: 32 x 21 = 672 and 42 / 7 = 6. Then subtract: 672 - 6 = 666, following the BODMAS order.

mcqs.q: In the question 60 + (72 / 7 of 3 + 5) x 2, what is 72 / (7 of 3)? (The book answer key prints 1 for the full question.)
mcqs.why: First do of: 7 of 3 means 7 x 3 = 21. Then 21 x 3 = 63 and 63 + 9 = 72, so 72 divided by 21 gives quotient 3 and remainder 9, not a whole number. The book answer key printing 1 is a misprint, because the division does not come out exact.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 100 of (3 x 150 / 10) = ?
mcqs.why: Inside the bracket, work left to right: 3 x 150 = 450, and then 450 / 10 = 45. The word of means multiply, so at last 100 x 45 = 4,500.

lessons.title: Exercise 1.8 — Distributive Laws
lessons.notes_html:
The Distributive Law

The distributive law says that multiplying a number by a sum or a difference gives the same answer as multiplying it by each part separately.

  • For addition: a x (b + c) = (a x b) + (a x c).
  • For subtraction: a x (b - c) = (a x b) - (a x c).
  • Check: 5 x (3 + 2) = 25, and (5 x 3) + (5 x 2) = 15 + 10 = 25, so both sides are equal.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: 5 x (3 + 2) = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 5 over the bracket: 5 x 3 = 15 and 5 x 2 = 10, and then 15 + 10 = 25. Check the other way: 3 + 2 = 5, and 5 x 5 = 25.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: 4 x (9 - 5) = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 4 over the bracket: 4 x 9 = 36 and 4 x 5 = 20, and then 36 - 20 = 16. Check the other way: 9 - 5 = 4, and 4 x 4 = 16.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: (18 + 2) x 10 = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 10 over the bracket: 18 x 10 = 180 and 2 x 10 = 20, and then 180 + 20 = 200. Check the other way: 18 + 2 = 20, and 20 x 10 = 200.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: 10 x (12 - 3) = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 10 over the bracket: 10 x 12 = 120 and 10 x 3 = 30, and then 120 - 30 = 90. Check the other way: 12 - 3 = 9, and 10 x 9 = 90.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 9 x (13 - ___) = (9 x 13) - (9 x 5)
mcqs.why: In the distributive law the same second number appears inside the bracket and in the last part on the right. Since the right side ends with 9 x 5, the blank inside the bracket must be 5.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: (30 + 40) x 10 = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 10 over the bracket: 30 x 10 = 300 and 40 x 10 = 400, and then 300 + 400 = 700. This matches the fill-in-the-blank form (___ + ___) x 10 in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Verify: 2 x (4 + 7) = (2 x 4) + (2 x 7). What is the value of each side?
mcqs.why: Left side: 4 + 7 = 11, and then 2 x 11 = 22. Right side: 2 x 4 = 8 and 2 x 7 = 14, and then 8 + 14 = 22. Both sides are equal, so the law is verified.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: 15 x (5 + 3) = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 15 over the bracket: 15 x 5 = 75 and 15 x 3 = 45, and then 75 + 45 = 120. Check the other way: 5 + 3 = 8, and 15 x 8 = 120.

mcqs.q: Solve: 10 x (20 - 3) = ? (In the book this fill-in item prints the last part as (___ x 30).)
mcqs.why: The correct distributive form is 10 x (20 - 3) = (10 x 20) - (10 x 3). Now 10 x 20 = 200 and 10 x 3 = 30, and then 200 - 30 = 170. The book printing the last part as (___ x 30) is a misprint: it should be (10 x 3), whose value is 30.

mcqs.q: Solve using the distributive law: (25 - 18) x 32 = ?
mcqs.why: Distribute the 32 over the bracket: 25 x 32 = 800 and 18 x 32 = 576, and then 800 - 576 = 224. Check the other way: 25 - 18 = 7, and 7 x 32 = 224.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 1

This review mixes all the skills of the unit: reading and writing numbers, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, the BODMAS order and the distributive law.

Quick Reminders

  • Read big numbers in groups of millions, thousands and ones.
  • Check a division by multiplying back, for example 822 x 30 = 24,660.
  • In BODMAS, do brackets and of before dividing, multiplying, adding and subtracting.

mcqs.q: How is 246,416,279 written in words?
options: Two hundred forty six million four hundred sixty thousand two hundred seventy nine
Two hundred forty six million four hundred sixteen thousand two hundred seventy nine
Two hundred forty six million four hundred sixty one thousand two hundred seventy nine
Twenty four million six hundred forty one thousand six hundred twenty nine
mcqs.why: The groups are 246 million, 416 thousand and 279 ones, read as two hundred forty six million four hundred sixteen thousand two hundred seventy nine.

mcqs.q: Write in numerals: Seventy five million, twenty six thousand four hundred twenty.
mcqs.why: Put the parts together group by group: the parts 75,000,000, 26,000 and 420 together make 75,026,420. The thousands group is 026, so a zero is written before 26.
Add in columns from the right, carrying where needed: 205,617,291 + 5,412,306 = 211,029,597. Check the ones column: 1 + 6 = 7, matching the last digit 7.
Subtract in columns from the right, borrowing where needed: 624,005,123 - 412,326,917 = 211,678,206. Borrowing across the zeros in the top number is the tricky part.
Multiplying by 10 puts one zero at the end of the number: 1,243 x 10 = 12,430. The digits stay the same and shift one place to the left.
Multiplying by 1,000 puts three zeros at the end of the number: 405,617 x 1,000 = 405,617,000. Count the zeros in 1,000 and add the same number of zeros.
By long division the quotient is 25,113. Check: 30 x 25,113 = 753,390, and then 753,390 + 10 = 753,400, so the remainder is 10.

mcqs.q: A water tanker holds 24,541 litres. How much water will 35 such tankers hold?
mcqs.why: Multiply using partial products: 24,541 x 30 = 736,230 and 24,541 x 5 = 122,705, and then 736,230 + 122,705 = 858,935 litres of water in 35 tankers.

mcqs.q: A box contains 30 chalks. How many boxes are needed to pack 24,660 chalks?
mcqs.why: Divide the total chalks by the number in one box: 24,660 / 30 = 822. Check by multiplying back: 822 x 30 = 24,660, so 822 boxes are needed.

mcqs.q: Solve using BODMAS: 48 - (5 of 2 + 12) = ?
mcqs.why: Do the bracket first, with of before addition: 5 of 2 means 5 x 2 = 10, and then 10 + 12 = 22. At last subtract: 48 - 22 = 26.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1 — HCF (by Prime Factorization and Division Method)
lessons.notes_html:
What is HCF?

The HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers exactly, with no remainder.

Method 1: Prime Factorization

  • Write each number as a product of prime factors.
  • Pick the prime factors that are common to all the numbers.
  • Multiply the common factors. The answer is the HCF.

Example: 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 28 = 2 × 2 × 7; the common factors are 2 × 2; 2 × 2 = 4; so the HCF of 16 and 28 is 4.

Method 2: Division Method

  • Divide the greater number by the smaller number.
  • Now divide the divisor by the remainder.
  • Keep going until the remainder is 0. The last divisor is the HCF.

Example: 70 ÷ 28 = 2 with remainder 14; 28 ÷ 14 = 2 with remainder 0; so the HCF of 28 and 70 is 14.

For three numbers, first find the HCF of two numbers, then find the HCF of that answer and the third number.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 16 and 28 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 16 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 28 = 2 × 2 × 7; the common prime factors are 2 × 2; 2 × 2 = 4; so the HCF is 4.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 44 and 66 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 44 = 2 × 2 × 11; 66 = 2 × 3 × 11; the common prime factors are 2 × 11; 2 × 11 = 22; so the HCF is 22.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 20, 60 and 80 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 20 = 2 × 2 × 5; 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 80 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; the factors common to all three are 2 × 2 × 5; 2 × 2 × 5 = 20; so the HCF is 20.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 35, 49 and 63 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 35 = 5 × 7; 49 = 7 × 7; 63 = 3 × 3 × 7; the only prime factor common to all three numbers is 7; so the HCF is 7.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 28 and 70 by the division method.
mcqs.why: Divide the greater number by the smaller number: 70 ÷ 28 = 2 with remainder 14; then 28 ÷ 14 = 2 with remainder 0; the last divisor is 14; so the HCF is 14.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 57 and 95 by the division method.
mcqs.why: 95 ÷ 57 = 1 with remainder 38; 57 ÷ 38 = 1 with remainder 19; 38 ÷ 19 = 2 with remainder 0; the last divisor is 19; so the HCF is 19.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 36, 60 and 96 by the division method.
mcqs.why: First find the HCF of 36 and 60: 60 ÷ 36 = 1 with remainder 24; 36 ÷ 24 = 1 with remainder 12; 24 ÷ 12 = 2 with remainder 0; so the HCF is 12; then 96 ÷ 12 = 8 with remainder 0; so the HCF of all three numbers is 12.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 52 and 78 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 52 = 2 × 2 × 13; 78 = 2 × 3 × 13; the common prime factors are 2 × 13; 2 × 13 = 26; so the HCF is 26.

mcqs.q: Find the HCF of 32, 48 and 96 by prime factorization.
Find the HCF of 54 and 90 by the division method.
mcqs.why: 90 ÷ 54 = 1 with remainder 36; 54 ÷ 36 = 1 with remainder 18; 36 ÷ 18 = 2 with remainder 0; the last divisor is 18; so the HCF is 18.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2 — LCM (by Prime Factorization and Division Method)
lessons.notes_html:
What is LCM?

The LCM (Lowest Common Multiple) is the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. Every number in the question divides the LCM exactly.

Method 1: Prime Factorization

  • Write each number as a product of prime factors.
  • Take the highest power of every prime factor that appears.
  • Multiply all these highest powers. The answer is the LCM.

Example: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3; the highest powers are 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 × 3; 4 × 27 = 108; so the LCM of 36 and 54 is 108.

Method 2: Division Method

  • Write all the numbers in one row.
  • Divide the row by a prime number that divides at least two of the numbers. Carry down any number that does not divide.
  • Keep dividing until every number in the row becomes 1.
  • Multiply all the divisors. The product is the LCM.

Example: dividing 16 and 24 again and again by 2 and then by 3 gives the divisors 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48; so the LCM of 16 and 24 is 48.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 36 and 54 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3; take the highest power of each prime: 2 × 2 and 3 × 3 × 3; 4 × 27 = 108; so the LCM is 108.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 33 and 55 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 33 = 3 × 11; 55 = 5 × 11; take every prime factor once at its highest power: 3 × 5 × 11; 3 × 5 × 11 = 165; so the LCM is 165.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 16, 24 and 40 by prime factorization.
Find the LCM of 25, 50 and 75 by prime factorization.
mcqs.why: 25 = 5 × 5; 50 = 2 × 5 × 5; 75 = 3 × 5 × 5; the highest powers are 2 and 3 and 5 × 5; 2 × 3 × 25 = 150; so the LCM is 150.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 16 and 24 by the division method.
mcqs.why: Divide 16 and 24 by 2 again and again, and then by 3 once; the divisors are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 48; so the LCM is 48.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 20 and 25 by the division method.
mcqs.why: 20 = 2 × 2 × 5; 25 = 5 × 5; the highest powers are 2 × 2 and 5 × 5; 4 × 25 = 100; so the LCM is 100.

mcqs.q: Find the LCM of 48, 64 and 96 by the division method.
Find the LCM of 15, 25, 30 and 45 by prime factorization.
Find the LCM of 36 and 48 by the division method.
mcqs.why: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 48 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; the highest powers are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 and 3 × 3; 16 × 9 = 144; so the LCM is 144.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3 — Real Life Problems of HCF and LCM
lessons.notes_html:
Which one do I use?

Read the question carefully. The words in the question tell you whether to find the HCF or the LCM.

Use LCM when the question asks for the smallest or least number

  • The smallest number that is divisible by the given numbers.
  • The least number of things that can be shared out exactly.
  • When things happen again and again and meet together, like buses leaving after fixed hours or friends exercising after fixed days.
  • The shortest height or length where two stacks or rows become equal.

Use HCF when the question asks for the greatest or biggest measure

  • The greatest number that divides the given numbers exactly.
  • The widest strip, longest piece or biggest measure that fits exactly, with nothing left over.
  • The capacity of a measure that can measure each quantity an exact number of times.

Example for LCM: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; 18 = 2 × 3 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36; so stacks of 12 cm and 18 cm boxes first match at a height of 36 cm.

Example for HCF: 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 80 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; the common factors are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16; so cloth 64 cm and 80 cm wide can be cut into strips 16 cm wide.

mcqs.q: What is the lowest number which is divisible by 15, 25, 40 and 75?
mcqs.why: The lowest number divisible by all of them is their LCM: 15 = 3 × 5; 25 = 5 × 5; 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; 75 = 3 × 5 × 5; the highest powers are 2 × 2 × 2 and 3 and 5 × 5; 8 × 3 × 25 = 600; so the lowest number is 600.

mcqs.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 42, 66 and 78 exactly.
mcqs.why: The greatest dividing number is the HCF: 42 = 2 × 3 × 7; 66 = 2 × 3 × 11; 78 = 2 × 3 × 13; the common factors are 2 × 3; 2 × 3 = 6; so the greatest number is 6.

mcqs.q: Salam exercises after every 10 days and Nadeem after every 6 days. Both exercised today. After how many days will they exercise together again?
mcqs.why: They meet again after the LCM of 10 and 6 days: 10 = 2 × 5; 6 = 2 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 3 × 5 = 30; so they will exercise together again after 30 days.

mcqs.q: Hooria is thinking of a number that is divisible by both 15 and 21. What is the smallest possible number she could be thinking of?
mcqs.why: The smallest number divisible by both is the LCM: 15 = 3 × 5; 21 = 3 × 7; take each prime once at its highest power: 3 × 5 × 7; 3 × 5 × 7 = 105; so the smallest number is 105.

mcqs.q: Four vans leave Sukkur at the same time. They are seen again after 3 hours, 4 hours, 5 hours and 6 hours. After how many hours will all of them come together?
mcqs.why: All four vans come together after the LCM of 3, 4, 5 and 6 hours: 3 = 3; 4 = 2 × 2; 5 = 5; 6 = 2 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60; so they come together after 60 hours.

mcqs.q: Boxes that are 12 cm tall are stacked next to boxes that are 18 cm tall. What is the shortest height at which the two stacks will be the same height?
mcqs.why: The stacks first match at the LCM of 12 and 18: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; 18 = 2 × 3 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36; so the shortest equal height is 36 cm.

mcqs.q: Samina has two pieces of cloth, one 64 cm wide and the other 80 cm wide. She wants to cut both into strips of equal width that are as wide as possible. How wide should she cut the strips?
mcqs.why: The widest possible strip is the HCF of 64 and 80: 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 80 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; the common factors are 2 × 2 × 2 × 2; 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16; so each strip should be 16 cm wide.

mcqs.q: Three milk containers hold 30 litres, 40 litres and 50 litres. What is the capacity of a measuring utensil which can measure the milk in each container an exact number of times?
mcqs.why: The measure must divide all three amounts exactly, so find the HCF: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5; 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; 50 = 2 × 5 × 5; the common factors are 2 × 5; 2 × 5 = 10; so the utensil should hold 10 litres.

mcqs.q: Find the greatest length of a measuring stick which can be used to measure exactly 30 cm, 60 cm or 90 cm.
mcqs.why: The stick must measure all three lengths exactly, so find the HCF: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5; 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 90 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5; the common factors are 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 3 × 5 = 30; so the greatest stick length is 30 cm.

mcqs.q: Pencils come in packages of 10 and erasers in packages of 12. A shopkeeper wants the smallest number of pencils and erasers so that there is exactly 1 eraser per pencil. How many packages should he buy?
options: 5 packages of pencils and 6 packages of erasers
6 packages of pencils and 6 packages of erasers
6 packages of pencils and 5 packages of erasers
10 packages of pencils and 12 packages of erasers
mcqs.why: He needs the same number of pencils and erasers, so find the LCM of 10 and 12: 10 = 2 × 5; 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; the LCM is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60; packages of pencils: 60 ÷ 10 = 6; packages of erasers: 60 ÷ 12 = 5; so he buys 6 packages of pencils and 5 packages of erasers.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 2
lessons.notes_html:
Quick Revision: HCF

The HCF is the greatest number that divides all the given numbers exactly. By prime factorization, multiply only the prime factors common to all the numbers. By the division method, divide the greater number by the smaller number, then keep dividing the divisor by the remainder until the remainder is 0; the last divisor is the HCF.

Example: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; 18 = 2 × 3 × 3; the common factors are 2 × 3; 2 × 3 = 6; so the HCF of 12 and 18 is 6.

Quick Revision: LCM

The LCM is the smallest number that all the given numbers divide exactly. By prime factorization, take the highest power of every prime factor. By the division method, divide the row of numbers by prime numbers until all become 1, then multiply all the divisors.

Example: 6 = 2 × 3; 8 = 2 × 2 × 2; 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24; so the LCM of 6, 8 and 12 is 24.

Choosing HCF or LCM in Word Problems

  • Words like least, smallest and divisible by point to the LCM.
  • Words like greatest, biggest measure and divides exactly point to the HCF.
  • Numbers that share no common factor except 1 have HCF 1. Example: 3, 5 and 7 are all prime and different, so their HCF is 1.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 2, 4 and 10?
mcqs.why: 2 = 2; 4 = 2 × 2; 10 = 2 × 5; the only prime factor common to all three numbers is 2; so the HCF is 2.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 3, 6 and 9?
mcqs.why: 3 = 3; 6 = 2 × 3; 9 = 3 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 3 × 3; 2 × 3 × 3 = 18; so the LCM is 18.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 3, 5 and 7?
mcqs.why: 3 = 3; 5 = 5; 7 = 7; the three numbers are different primes, so they have no common prime factor at all; the only number that divides all of them is 1; so the HCF is 1.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 2, 3 and 5?
mcqs.why: 2, 3 and 5 are all prime numbers, so the LCM is their product: 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 3 × 5 = 30; so the LCM is 30.

mcqs.q: To find the HCF by the division method, we divide the greater number by the ____.
mcqs.why: In the division method we divide the greater number by the smaller number first; then we divide the divisor by the remainder again and again until the remainder is 0; the last divisor is the HCF.

mcqs.q: Find the least number which is exactly divisible by 6, 8 and 12.
mcqs.why: The least such number is the LCM: 6 = 2 × 3; 8 = 2 × 2 × 2; 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 2 × 3; 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24; so the least number is 24.

mcqs.q: Find the greatest number which divides 12 and 18 exactly.
mcqs.why: The greatest dividing number is the HCF: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3; 18 = 2 × 3 × 3; the common factors are 2 × 3; 2 × 3 = 6; so the greatest number is 6.

mcqs.q: What is the least number of apples which can be distributed equally among 10, 15 or 20 children?
mcqs.why: The number of apples must be divisible by 10, 15 and 20, so find the LCM: 10 = 2 × 5; 15 = 3 × 5; 20 = 2 × 2 × 5; the highest powers give 2 × 2 × 3 × 5; 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 60; so the least number is 60 apples.

mcqs.q: Two pieces of cloth are 15 metres and 20 metres long. They are to be cut into small pieces of equal length. What will be the greatest length of each piece?
mcqs.why: The greatest equal piece is the HCF of 15 and 20: 15 = 3 × 5; 20 = 2 × 2 × 5; the only common prime factor is 5; so the greatest length of each piece is 5 metres.

mcqs.q: What will be the capacity of the smallest drum which can be filled completely using each of the utensils that can fill exactly 15 litres, 25 litres, 40 litres or 75 litres?
mcqs.why: The drum capacity must be a multiple of all four amounts, so find the LCM: 15 = 3 × 5; 25 = 5 × 5; 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5; 75 = 3 × 5 × 5; the highest powers are 2 × 2 × 2 and 3 and 5 × 5; 8 × 3 × 25 = 600; so the smallest drum holds 600 litres.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1 — Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Adding fractions with different denominators

First find the LCM (lowest common multiple) of the denominators. Change each fraction into an equivalent fraction with the LCM as denominator. Then add the numerators and keep the same denominator. At the end, write the answer in lowest terms.

Subtracting fractions

Subtraction uses the same steps. Make the denominators the same with the LCM, then subtract the numerators. The bigger fraction must come first, otherwise the answer is negative.

Mixed numbers

A mixed number like 2 1/3 has a whole part and a fraction part. Before adding or subtracting, change it into an improper fraction: multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator.

Useful words

  • and between two fractions means add them.
  • from means subtract: subtract 2/3 from 3/4 means 3/4 minus 2/3.
  • For three fractions, take the LCM of all three denominators.

mcqs.why: The LCM of 3 and 2 is 6. Change both fractions: 1/3 = 2/6 and 1/2 = 3/6. Then add the numerators: 2/6 + 3/6 = 5/6.
The LCM of 4 and 8 is 8. Change 3/4 into 6/8, because 3 x 2 = 6 and 4 x 2 = 8. Then add: 6/8 + 1/8 = 7/8.
The LCM of 5 and 3 is 15. Change the fractions: 2/5 = 6/15 and 1/3 = 5/15. Then add the numerators: 6/15 + 5/15 = 11/15.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 3/4 - 3/8
mcqs.why: The LCM of 4 and 8 is 8. Change 3/4 into 6/8, because 3 x 2 = 6 and 4 x 2 = 8. Then subtract: 6/8 - 3/8 = 3/8.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 2/3 - 1/4
mcqs.why: The LCM of 3 and 4 is 12. Change the fractions: 2/3 = 8/12 and 1/4 = 3/12. Then subtract the numerators: 8/12 - 3/12 = 5/12.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 5/6 - 1/2
mcqs.why: The LCM of 6 and 2 is 6. Change 1/2 into 3/6. Then subtract: 5/6 - 3/6 = 2/6. In lowest terms, 2/6 = 1/3, so the answer is 1/3.
The LCM of 3, 5 and 9 is 45. The fractions become 15/45, 9/45 and 5/45. First 15/45 + 9/45 = 24/45. Then 24/45 + 5/45 = 29/45.

mcqs.q: Add 2/5 and 3/10
mcqs.why: The word and means add. The LCM of 5 and 10 is 10. Change 2/5 into 4/10, because 2 x 2 = 4 and 5 x 2 = 10. Then 4/10 + 3/10 = 7/10.

mcqs.q: Subtract 2/3 from 3/4
mcqs.why: From means subtract, so we find 3/4 - 2/3. The LCM of 4 and 3 is 12. The fractions become 9/12 and 8/12. Then 9/12 - 8/12 = 1/12.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 4 2/5 - 1 1/4
mcqs.why: Change the mixed numbers: 4 2/5 is 22/5 and 1 1/4 is 5/4. The LCM of 5 and 4 is 20, giving 88/20 and 25/20. Then 88/20 - 25/20 = 63/20, which is 3 3/20.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2 — Multiplication of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Fraction times a whole number

Multiply the whole number by the numerator only. The denominator stays the same. Then simplify the answer. For example, in 3/4 x 4, only the 3 is multiplied by 4.

Fraction times a fraction

Multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together. First change every mixed number into an improper fraction.

Cancelling

  • Cancelling means dividing a numerator and a denominator by the same number before multiplying. It makes the working small and easy.
  • The word of means multiply: 3 parts of 1/4 means 1/4 x 3.
  • Always write the final answer in lowest terms, and change an improper answer into a mixed number when needed.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 3/4 x 4
mcqs.why: Multiply the numerator by the whole number: 3 x 4 = 12, so we get 12/4. Then simplify: 12/4 = 3, because 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 1/3 x 6
mcqs.why: Multiply the numerator by the whole number: 1 x 6 = 6, so we get 6/3. Then simplify: 6/3 = 2, because 6 ÷ 3 = 2.

mcqs.q: Multiply: 3/5 x 11
mcqs.why: Multiply the numerator by the whole number: 3 x 11 = 33, so we get 33/5. Now 33 ÷ 5 gives 6 with remainder 3, so 33/5 is the mixed number 6 3/5.

mcqs.q: Multiply 1/2 by 1/5
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators together and denominators together: 1 x 1 = 1 and 2 x 5 = 10. So the product of the two fractions is 1/10.

mcqs.q: Multiply 1 1/4 by 3/4
mcqs.why: First change the mixed number: 1 1/4 is 5/4. Then multiply: 5 x 3 = 15 and 4 x 4 = 16. So the product is 15/16.

mcqs.q: Multiply 2 1/3 by 4/5
mcqs.why: First change the mixed number: 2 1/3 is 7/3. Then 7 x 4 = 28 and 3 x 5 = 15, giving 28/15. As a mixed number this is 1 13/15, because 28 - 15 = 13.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 3/4 x 8/9
mcqs.why: Multiply first: 3 x 8 = 24 and 4 x 9 = 36, giving 24/36. Divide the top and bottom by 12: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3. So the answer in lowest terms is 2/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 2/5 x 25/4
mcqs.why: Multiply: 2 x 25 = 50 and 5 x 4 = 20, giving 50/20. In lowest terms 50/20 = 5/2, and 5/2 written as a mixed number is 2 1/2.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 7/3 x 9/14
mcqs.why: Multiply: 7 x 9 = 63 and 3 x 14 = 42, giving 63/42. Divide the top and bottom by 21: 63 ÷ 21 = 3 and 42 ÷ 21 = 2. So we get 3/2, which is 1 1/2.

mcqs.q: Write 3 parts of 1/4 as a multiplication and solve it
mcqs.why: Parts of means multiply, so we find 1/4 x 3. The numerator becomes 1 x 3 = 3 and the denominator stays 4. So 3 parts of 1/4 make 3/4.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3 — Multiplication with Brackets
lessons.notes_html:
Brackets first

When a question has brackets, always solve the part inside the brackets first. After that, multiply the remaining fractions.

Steps for bracket questions

  • Change every mixed number into an improper fraction.
  • Solve the brackets: multiply numerators together and denominators together.
  • Cancel common factors whenever possible to keep numbers small.
  • Multiply the bracket answer by the fraction outside the brackets.

Grouping does not change the final product: the same three fractions multiplied in a different bracket order give the same answer.

mcqs.why: Change 2 1/4 into 9/4. Multiply all numerators: 5 x 9 = 45 and 45 x 16 = 720. Multiply all denominators: 6 x 4 = 24 and 24 x 5 = 120. Then 720 ÷ 120 = 6.
Brackets first: 2 1/4 is 9/4, and 9/4 x 8/7 = 18/7, because 9 x 8 = 72 and 4 x 7 = 28 and 72/28 simplifies to 18/7. Then 7/9 x 18/7 = 2, because 7 x 18 = 126 and 9 x 7 = 63 and 126 ÷ 63 = 2.
Brackets first: 4/5 x 10/3 = 8/3, because 4 x 10 = 40 and 5 x 3 = 15 and 40/15 simplifies to 8/3. Then 8/3 x 9/8 = 3, because 8 x 9 = 72 and 3 x 8 = 24 and 72 ÷ 24 = 3.
Brackets first: 3/4 x 16/5 = 12/5, because 3 x 16 = 48 and 4 x 5 = 20 and 48/20 simplifies to 12/5. Also 1 2/3 is 5/3. Then 12/5 x 5/3 = 4, because 12 x 5 = 60 and 5 x 3 = 15 and 60 ÷ 15 = 4.
Brackets first: 1 1/6 is 7/6, and 7/6 x 5/6 = 35/36, because 7 x 5 = 35 and 6 x 6 = 36. Also 5 1/7 is 36/7. Then 35/36 x 36/7 = 5, because the 36 cancels and 35 ÷ 7 = 5.

Brackets first: 12 1/2 is 25/2 and 1 11/21 is 32/21. Their product is 400/21, because 25 x 32 = 800 and 2 x 21 = 42 and 800/42 simplifies to 400/21. Also 1 5/16 is 21/16. Then 21/16 x 400/21 = 25, because the 21 cancels and 400 ÷ 16 = 25.

Brackets first: 1 3/17 is 20/17 and 2 1/10 is 21/10. Their product is 42/17, because 20 x 21 = 420 and 17 x 10 = 170 and 420/170 simplifies to 42/17. Also 2 5/6 is 17/6. Then 17/6 x 42/17 = 7, because the 17 cancels and 42 ÷ 6 = 7.
Brackets first: 3 9/10 is 39/10, and 39/10 x 20/36 = 13/6 after cancelling. Also 1 11/13 is 24/13. Then 13/6 x 24/13 = 4, because the 13 cancels and 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

Brackets first: 2 4/5 is 14/5 and 1 5/7 is 12/7. Their product is 24/5, because 14 x 12 = 168 and 5 x 7 = 35 and 168/35 simplifies to 24/5. Also 2 1/12 is 25/12. Then 24/5 x 25/12 = 10, because 24 x 25 = 600 and 5 x 12 = 60 and 600 ÷ 60 = 10.

Brackets first: 2 1/10 is 21/10, and 21/10 x 1/7 = 3/10, because 21 ÷ 7 = 3. Also 8 1/3 is 25/3. Then 25/3 x 3/10 = 5/2, because 25 x 3 = 75 and 3 x 10 = 30 and 75/30 simplifies to 5/2. The mixed number 5/2 is 2 1/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4 — Verify the Distributive Laws
lessons.notes_html:
The distributive law over addition

The distributive law says that multiplying a fraction by a sum gives the same answer as multiplying it by each part and then adding. In symbols with words: a times (b plus c) is the same as (a times b) plus (a times c).

The distributive law over subtraction

The same law works for subtraction: a times (b minus c) is the same as (a times b) minus (a times c).

How to verify a law

  • Solve the left hand side (LHS) on its own: brackets first, then multiply.
  • Solve the right hand side (RHS) on its own: multiply each part, then add or subtract.
  • If LHS and RHS give the same value, the law is verified.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 2/5 x (3/7 + 4/5)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 7 and 5 is 35, so 3/7 + 4/5 = 43/35, because 15/35 + 28/35 = 43/35. Then multiply: 2 x 43 = 86 and 5 x 35 = 175, giving 86/175.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 7/9 x (1/4 + 1/3)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 4 and 3 is 12, so 1/4 + 1/3 = 7/12, because 3/12 + 4/12 = 7/12. Then multiply: 7 x 7 = 49 and 9 x 12 = 108, giving 49/108.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 2/7 x (3/8 + 1/5)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 8 and 5 is 40, so 3/8 + 1/5 = 23/40, because 15/40 + 8/40 = 23/40. Then 2 x 23 = 46 and 7 x 40 = 280, and 46/280 simplifies to 23/140. Note: the book prints the first part of the right hand side wrongly as (2/7 + 3/8) with a plus sign; it should be (2/7 x 3/8), and with that correction both sides are equal.

mcqs.q: Find the value of (1/9 + 4/9) x 3/4
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the denominators are already the same, so 1/9 + 4/9 = 5/9. Then multiply: 5 x 3 = 15 and 9 x 4 = 36, giving 15/36. In lowest terms 15/36 = 5/12.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 1/2 x (3/4 - 2/3)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 4 and 3 is 12, so 3/4 - 2/3 = 1/12, because 9/12 - 8/12 = 1/12. Then multiply: 1/2 x 1/12 = 1/24, because 1 x 1 = 1 and 2 x 12 = 24.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 1/5 x (1/2 - 1/3)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 2 and 3 is 6, so 1/2 - 1/3 = 1/6, because 3/6 - 2/6 = 1/6. Then multiply: 1/5 x 1/6 = 1/30, because 1 x 1 = 1 and 5 x 6 = 30.

mcqs.q: Find the value of (4/5 - 3/4) x 2/3
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 5 and 4 is 20, so 4/5 - 3/4 = 1/20, because 16/20 - 15/20 = 1/20. Then multiply: 1/20 x 2/3 = 2/60, and 2/60 in lowest terms is 1/30.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 5/6 x (4/7 - 1/2)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 7 and 2 is 14, so 4/7 - 1/2 = 1/14, because 8/14 - 7/14 = 1/14. Then multiply: 5 x 1 = 5 and 6 x 14 = 84, giving 5/84.

mcqs.q: Using the distributive law, 1/2 x (1/4 + 1/4) is equal to (1/2 x 1/4) + (1/2 x 1/4). What is its value?
mcqs.why: Left side: brackets first, 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4, and 2/4 = 1/2. Then 1/2 x 1/2 = 1/4. Right side check: 1/2 x 1/4 = 1/8, and 1/8 + 1/8 = 2/8, and 2/8 = 1/4. Both sides match.

mcqs.q: Find the value of 3/4 x (2/5 + 1/5)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the denominators are already the same, so 2/5 + 1/5 = 3/5. Then multiply: 3 x 3 = 9 and 4 x 5 = 20, giving 9/20. Checking by the law: 3/4 x 2/5 = 6/20 and 3/4 x 1/5 = 3/20, and 6/20 + 3/20 = 9/20.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.5 — Word Problems on Multiplication
lessons.notes_html:
Reading a word problem

Find the words that tell the operation. The word of usually means multiply: 1/8 of a length means 1/8 times that length. A part of a whole amount is found by multiplying the fraction by the whole amount.

Useful facts

  • One dozen means 12 things, so 13 dozen eggs means 13 x 12 eggs.
  • Change a mixed number into an improper fraction before multiplying.
  • For questions like present students, first find the part on leave, then subtract it from the total.
  • Always write the unit in the answer, like metres, kilograms or rupees.

mcqs.q: The height of a door is 2 2/3 metres. 1/8 part of it was trimmed off. How much was trimmed off?
mcqs.why: Trimmed part means 1/8 of 2 2/3. Change 2 2/3 into 8/3. Then multiply: 8/3 x 1/8 = 1/3, because the 8 cancels. So 1/3 metre was trimmed off.

mcqs.q: One-tenth of the students of a school were on leave. If 550 students are enrolled, how many students were present?
mcqs.why: Students on leave: 1/10 x 550 = 55, because 550 ÷ 10 = 55. Students present: 550 - 55 = 495. So 495 students were present in school.

mcqs.q: A hospital needs 12 drips of dextrose solution but has only 2/3 of the required amount. How many drips are available?
mcqs.why: Available drips means 2/3 of 12. Multiply: 12 x 2/3 = 8, because 12 x 2 = 24 and 24 ÷ 3 = 8. So the hospital has 8 drips available.

mcqs.q: A lady uses 1/5 of 50 kg of wheat to make bread once. If she makes bread twice a day, how much wheat is used in a day?
mcqs.why: Wheat used once: 1/5 x 50 = 10, because 50 ÷ 5 = 10. She makes bread twice, so the daily use is 10 x 2 = 20. So 20 kg of wheat is used in a day.

mcqs.q: The price of one egg is Rs 9 1/2. Find the price of 13 dozen eggs.
mcqs.why: First, 13 dozen means 13 x 12 = 156 eggs. One egg costs 19/2 rupees, because 9 1/2 is 19/2. Total price: 156 x 19/2 = 1482, because 156 ÷ 2 = 78 and 78 x 19 = 1482 rupees.

mcqs.q: A lady bought 5 2/5 metres of cloth and used 1/3 of it for a TV cover. How much cloth did she use?
mcqs.why: Cloth used means 1/3 of 5 2/5. Change 5 2/5 into 27/5. Then 1/3 x 27/5 = 27/15, because 27 ÷ 3 = 9 gives 9/5 after cancelling. The mixed number 9/5 is 1 4/5 metres.

mcqs.q: A cooler holds 8 bottles of water. Each bottle holds 2 1/2 litres. What is the capacity of the full cooler?
mcqs.why: Capacity means 8 times one bottle. Change 2 1/2 into 5/2. Then multiply: 8 x 5/2 = 20, because 8 x 5 = 40 and 40 ÷ 2 = 20. So the full cooler holds 20 litres.

mcqs.q: A cloth consists of 12 pieces, and each piece is 1 1/2 metres long. What is the total length of the cloth?
mcqs.why: Total length means 12 times one piece. Change 1 1/2 into 3/2. Then multiply: 12 x 3/2 = 18, because 12 x 3 = 36 and 36 ÷ 2 = 18. So the total length is 18 metres.

mcqs.q: The cost of 1 kg of potatoes is Rs 45. Find the cost of 15 2/4 kg of potatoes.
mcqs.why: Change the weight: 15 2/4 is 31/2 kg. Cost means multiply: 45 x 31/2 = 697.50, because 45 x 31 = 1395 and 1395 ÷ 2 = 697.5. So the cost is Rs 697.50.

mcqs.q: One small piece of wire is 8 1/3 metres long. Find the total length of 13 1/5 such pieces.
mcqs.why: Change both mixed numbers: 8 1/3 is 25/3 and 13 1/5 is 66/5. Multiply: 25 x 66 = 1650 and 3 x 5 = 15, giving 1650/15. Then 1650 ÷ 15 = 110. So the total length is 110 metres.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.6 — Reciprocals and Division
lessons.notes_html:
What is a reciprocal?

The reciprocal of a fraction is made by turning it upside down: the numerator and denominator change places. For a whole number, first write it over 1: the reciprocal of 4 is 1/4. For a mixed number, first change it into an improper fraction, then turn it upside down.

Dividing by a number

  • To divide a fraction by a whole number or by another number, change the division into multiplication by the reciprocal of the second number.
  • The first fraction stays the same. Only the divisor is flipped.
  • Cancel and simplify, and write the answer in lowest terms.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of 2?
mcqs.why: Write the whole number as a fraction: 2 = 2/1. Now turn it upside down, so the numerator and denominator change places. The reciprocal of 2/1 is 1/2.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of 1/5?
mcqs.why: Turn the fraction upside down: the numerator 1 and the denominator 5 change places. So 1/5 becomes 5/1, and 5/1 is simply the whole number 5.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of 3/4?
mcqs.why: In a reciprocal, the numerator and denominator change places. The numerator 3 goes to the bottom and the denominator 4 comes to the top, so 3/4 becomes 4/3.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of 2 1/3?
mcqs.why: First change the mixed number into an improper fraction: 2 1/3 is 7/3, because 2 x 3 = 6 and 6 + 1 = 7. Now turn 7/3 upside down. The reciprocal is 3/7.

mcqs.q: What is the reciprocal of 4 2/3?
mcqs.why: First change the mixed number into an improper fraction: 4 2/3 is 14/3, because 4 x 3 = 12 and 12 + 2 = 14. Now turn 14/3 upside down. The reciprocal is 3/14.
Change division into multiplication by the reciprocal of 5/6, which is 6/5. So 1/2 x 6/5 = 6/10, because 1 x 6 = 6 and 2 x 5 = 10. In lowest terms, 6/10 = 3/5.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2/3 ÷ 4
mcqs.why: The reciprocal of 4 is 1/4. Change the division into multiplication: 2/3 x 1/4 = 2/12, because 2 x 1 = 2 and 3 x 4 = 12. In lowest terms, 2/12 = 1/6.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3/4 ÷ 6
mcqs.why: The reciprocal of 6 is 1/6. Change the division into multiplication: 3/4 x 1/6 = 3/24, because 3 x 1 = 3 and 4 x 6 = 24. In lowest terms, 3/24 = 1/8.

mcqs.q: Solve: 7/8 ÷ 14
mcqs.why: The reciprocal of 14 is 1/14. Change the division into multiplication: 7/8 x 1/14 = 7/112, because 7 x 1 = 7 and 8 x 14 = 112. In lowest terms, 7/112 = 1/16, because 112 ÷ 7 = 16.

mcqs.q: Solve: 3 1/3 ÷ 5
mcqs.why: Change the mixed number: 3 1/3 is 10/3. The reciprocal of 5 is 1/5. Multiply: 10/3 x 1/5 = 10/15, because 10 x 1 = 10 and 3 x 5 = 15. In lowest terms, 10/15 = 2/3.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.7 — Dividing a Fraction by a Fraction
lessons.notes_html:
The rule for dividing fractions

To divide a fraction by a fraction, keep the first fraction the same, change the division sign into multiplication, and flip the second fraction into its reciprocal. Then multiply numerators together and denominators together.

Steps

  • Change any mixed number into an improper fraction first.
  • Take the reciprocal of the divisor only, never of the first fraction.
  • Cancel common factors where possible, then multiply.
  • Simplify the answer and write it as a mixed number if it is improper.

A fraction divided by itself always gives 1, and dividing by a smaller fraction gives a bigger answer.

mcqs.why: Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 3/4 is 4/3. Multiply: 1/2 x 4/3 = 4/6, because 1 x 4 = 4 and 2 x 3 = 6. In lowest terms, 4/6 = 2/3.
Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 4/9 is 9/4. Multiply: 7/6 x 9/4 = 63/24, because 7 x 9 = 63 and 6 x 4 = 24. Simplify: 63/24 = 21/8, which is the mixed number 2 5/8.
Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 15/16 is 16/15. Multiply: 3/4 x 16/15 = 48/60, because 3 x 16 = 48 and 4 x 15 = 60. In lowest terms, 48/60 = 4/5.
Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 1/12 is 12/1, which is 12. Multiply: 1/6 x 12/1 = 12/6, because 1 x 12 = 12 and 6 x 1 = 6. Then 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 4/3 is 3/4. Multiply: 16/9 x 3/4 = 48/36, because 16 x 3 = 48 and 9 x 4 = 36. Simplify: 48/36 = 4/3 in lowest terms, and 4/3 written as a mixed number is 1 1/3.
Change the mixed number: 1 1/4 is 5/4. Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 1/4 is 4/1. Multiply: 5/4 x 4/1 = 20/4, because 5 x 4 = 20 and 4 x 1 = 4. Then 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
Change both mixed numbers: 8 1/2 is 17/2 and 3 1/2 is 7/2. Flip the divisor: the reciprocal of 7/2 is 2/7. Multiply: 17/2 x 2/7 = 17/7, because the 2 cancels. The mixed number for 17/7 is 2 3/7.

Change both mixed numbers: 2 1/5 is 11/5 and 1 1/6 is 7/6. Flip the divisor: the reciprocal of 7/6 is 6/7. Multiply: 11/5 x 6/7 = 66/35, because 11 x 6 = 66 and 5 x 7 = 35. The mixed number for 66/35 is 1 31/35.

Change both mixed numbers: 3 8/9 is 35/9 and 1 1/9 is 10/9. Flip the divisor: the reciprocal of 10/9 is 9/10. Multiply: 35/9 x 9/10 = 35/10, because the 9 cancels. Simplify: 35/10 = 7/2, which is 3 1/2.
Flip the second fraction: the reciprocal of 40/30 is 30/40. Multiply: 20/30 x 30/40 = 600/1200, because 20 x 30 = 600 and 30 x 40 = 1200. In lowest terms, 600/1200 = 1/2.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.8 — Word Problems on Division
lessons.notes_html:
When a word problem needs division

Division is used when a total amount is shared equally, or when we ask how many small parts fit into a bigger amount. The price of 1 kg, the cloth for 1 dress and the distance in 1 hour are all found by division.

Steps

  • Write the division with the total first and the number of parts second.
  • Change mixed numbers into improper fractions.
  • Multiply by the reciprocal of the second fraction and simplify.
  • Sometimes the word of appears instead: one-fifth of 35 cars is a multiplication, not a division. Read the question carefully.

mcqs.q: Talib buys 10 1/2 kg of tomatoes for Rs 210. What is the price of 1 kg of tomatoes?
mcqs.why: Price of 1 kg means divide the total price by the weight: 210 ÷ 21/2, because 10 1/2 is 21/2. Multiply by the reciprocal: 210 x 2/21 = 420/21, and 420 ÷ 21 = 20. So 1 kg costs Rs 20.

mcqs.q: One-fifth of the 35 cars in a parking area are blue. How many blue cars are there?
mcqs.why: One-fifth of 35 is a multiplication here, because of means multiply. So 1/5 x 35 = 7, because 35 ÷ 5 = 7. There are 7 blue cars in the parking area.

mcqs.q: Naila has a 7/3 m piece of lace. She cuts it into small pieces of length 1/12 m each. How many pieces can she make?
mcqs.why: Number of pieces means divide the total length by the length of one piece: 7/3 ÷ 1/12. Multiply by the reciprocal: 7/3 x 12/1 = 84/3, because 7 x 12 = 84. Then 84 ÷ 3 = 28 pieces.

mcqs.q: A camp cook made 1 3/4 kg of baked beans. Each serving is 1/4 kg. How many servings did the cook make?
mcqs.why: Number of servings means divide: 1 3/4 ÷ 1/4. Change 1 3/4 into 7/4. Multiply by the reciprocal of 1/4: 7/4 x 4/1 = 28/4, and 28 ÷ 4 = 7. So the cook made 7 servings.

mcqs.q: A road is 50 1/2 metres long. Half of it was damaged in rain. How much of the road is safe?
mcqs.why: The safe part is the other half, so find half of 50 1/2. Change it into 101/2 and divide by 2: 101/2 x 1/2 = 101/4, because 101 x 1 = 101 and 2 x 2 = 4. The mixed number for 101/4 is 25 1/4 metres.

mcqs.q: Rehan bought 82 1/2 metres of cloth to make uniforms for 15 children of equal size. How much cloth is used in each dress?
mcqs.why: Cloth for each dress means divide equally: 82 1/2 ÷ 15. Change 82 1/2 into 165/2. Multiply by the reciprocal of 15: 165/2 x 1/15 = 165/30, and 165/30 simplifies to 11/2, which is 5 1/2 metres.

mcqs.q: A plastic drum holds 49 1/2 litres of water. How many bottles holding 1 1/2 litres each can be filled from it?
mcqs.why: Number of bottles means divide: 49 1/2 ÷ 1 1/2. Change them into 99/2 and 3/2. Multiply by the reciprocal: 99/2 x 2/3 = 198/6, because 99 x 2 = 198 and 2 x 3 = 6. Then 198 ÷ 6 = 33 bottles.

mcqs.q: A boy completes 8 3/4 km in 2 1/2 hours on a bicycle. How much distance does he complete in 1 hour?
mcqs.why: Distance in 1 hour means divide: 8 3/4 ÷ 2 1/2. Change them into 35/4 and 5/2. Multiply by the reciprocal: 35/4 x 2/5 = 70/20, because 35 x 2 = 70 and 4 x 5 = 20. Simplify: 70/20 = 7/2, which is 3 1/2 km.

mcqs.q: A cook made 2 1/4 kg of baked beans. Each serving is 1/4 kg. How many servings did the cook make?
mcqs.why: Number of servings means divide: 2 1/4 ÷ 1/4. Change 2 1/4 into 9/4. Multiply by the reciprocal of 1/4: 9/4 x 4/1 = 36/4, and 36 ÷ 4 = 9. So the cook made 9 servings.

mcqs.q: 82 1/2 metres of cloth is shared equally among 10 children for uniforms. How much cloth is used in each dress?
mcqs.why: Cloth for each dress means divide equally: 82 1/2 ÷ 10. Change 82 1/2 into 165/2. Multiply by the reciprocal of 10: 165/2 x 1/10 = 165/20, and 165/20 simplifies to 33/4, which is 8 1/4 metres.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.9 — Simplify Fractions Using BODMAS Rule
lessons.notes_html:
The BODMAS rule

BODMAS tells the order of operations: Brackets first, then Of, then Division, then Multiplication, then Addition, and Subtraction last.

How to simplify

  • Solve the brackets first, working from the innermost bracket outwards.
  • The word of means multiply, and it is done before ordinary multiplication.
  • Division and multiplication come before addition and subtraction.
  • Change mixed numbers into improper fractions and use the LCM when adding or subtracting.

If the order is wrong, the answer is wrong, so follow BODMAS step by step.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 3/4 + 2/9 x 4 1/3 ÷ 3 1/4
mcqs.why: Division and multiplication come before addition. Change 4 1/3 into 13/3 and 3 1/4 into 13/4. Dividing by 13/4 means multiplying by 4/13, and the 13 cancels: 2/9 x 4 = 8/9, then 8/9 ÷ 3 = 8/27. Now add with LCM 108: 3/4 + 8/27 = 113/108, because 81/108 + 32/108 = 113/108. The mixed number is 1 5/108.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 1/4 x (8/3 + 2/7)
mcqs.why: Brackets first: the LCM of 3 and 7 is 21, so 8/3 + 2/7 = 62/21, because 56/21 + 6/21 = 62/21. Then multiply: 1/4 x 62/21 = 62/84, because 1 x 62 = 62 and 4 x 21 = 84. In lowest terms, 62/84 = 31/42.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 1/2 + (3/4 x 1 7/33 - 1/3)
mcqs.why: Inside the bracket, multiplication comes first. Change 1 7/33 into 40/33. Then 3/4 x 40/33 = 10/11 after cancelling. Next 10/11 - 1/3 = 19/33, because 30/33 - 11/33 = 19/33. Finally add with LCM 66: 1/2 + 19/33 = 71/66, because 33/66 + 38/66 = 71/66. The mixed number is 1 5/66.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: (3 1/6 - 1 1/4) x 2
mcqs.why: Brackets first. Change the mixed numbers: 3 1/6 is 19/6 and 1 1/4 is 5/4. With LCM 12: 19/6 - 5/4 = 23/12, because 38/12 - 15/12 = 23/12. Then multiply by 2: 23/12 x 2 = 23/6, which is the mixed number 3 5/6.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: (4/5 - 3/10) x (1/2 + 3/4)
mcqs.why: Solve both brackets first. First bracket: 4/5 - 3/10 = 1/2, because 8/10 - 3/10 = 5/10 and 5/10 = 1/2. Second bracket: 1/2 + 3/4 = 5/4, because 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4. Then multiply: 1/2 x 5/4 = 5/8.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: (2 1/2 ÷ 3/4) x 3/7 - (1/4 + 1/8)
mcqs.why: Start with the division: 2 1/2 is 5/2, and 5/2 ÷ 3/4 = 10/3, because 5/2 x 4/3 = 20/6 and 20/6 = 10/3. Then 10/3 x 3/7 = 10/7, because the 3 cancels. The bracket is 1/4 + 1/8 = 3/8, because 2/8 + 1/8 = 3/8. Finally 10/7 - 3/8 = 59/56, because 80/56 - 21/56 = 59/56. The mixed number is 1 3/56.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 1 3/5 x (4/3 - 3/4 + 2 1/3) ÷ 1 2/7
mcqs.why: Brackets first with LCM 12: 4/3 - 3/4 + 2 1/3 is 35/12, because 16/12 - 9/12 = 7/12 and 7/12 + 28/12 = 35/12, using 2 1/3 is 7/3 = 28/12. Change 1 3/5 into 8/5: 8/5 x 35/12 = 14/3 after cancelling. Change 1 2/7 into 9/7 and divide: 14/3 ÷ 9/7 = 98/27, because 14/3 x 7/9 = 98/27 and 14 x 7 = 98. The mixed number is 3 17/27.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: (5/4 + 8/3) x (10/3 + 5/2)
mcqs.why: Solve both brackets first. First bracket with LCM 12: 5/4 + 8/3 = 47/12, because 15/12 + 32/12 = 47/12. Second bracket with LCM 6: 10/3 + 5/2 = 35/6, because 20/6 + 15/6 = 35/6. Then multiply: 47/12 x 35/6 = 1645/72, because 47 x 35 = 1645 and 12 x 6 = 72. The mixed number is 22 61/72.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 20 + 5 of 9 - (1 2/3 x 1/5)
mcqs.why: Of comes before addition: 5 of 9 means 5 x 9 = 45. The bracket: 1 2/3 is 5/3, and 5/3 x 1/5 = 1/3, because the 5 cancels. Now work from the left: 20 + 45 = 65. Finally subtract 1/3 from 65 to get 64 2/3, because 65 = 64 3/3 and 3/3 - 1/3 = 2/3.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 4 1/2 + (5 1/3 of 3) - 2 2/3
mcqs.why: Of comes first inside the bracket: 5 1/3 is 16/3, and 16/3 of 3 means 16/3 x 3 = 16, because the 3 cancels. Now use LCM 6: 4 1/2 is 9/2 = 27/6, the 16 is 96/6, and 2 2/3 is 8/3 = 16/6. First 27/6 + 96/6 = 123/6. Then 123/6 - 16/6 = 107/6. The mixed number is 17 5/6.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 3
lessons.notes_html:
Review of fractions

A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part, while an improper fraction has a numerator bigger than its denominator. Fractions like 1/3, 2/6 and 3/9 are equivalent fractions because they show the same value.

Key facts to remember

  • The lowest form of a fraction is found by dividing the numerator and denominator by their highest common factor.
  • The reciprocal of a mixed number is found after changing it into an improper fraction.
  • One dozen is 12, one metre is 100 cm, and the word of means multiply.
  • Sharing a total equally, or finding how many small parts fit into a total, is done by division.

mcqs.q: Five ball points are bought for Rs 50 3/4. Find the price of one ball point.
mcqs.why: Price of one means divide the total price by 5: 50 3/4 ÷ 5. Change 50 3/4 into 203/4. Multiply by the reciprocal of 5: 203/4 x 1/5 = 203/20, because 203 x 1 = 203 and 4 x 5 = 20. The mixed number for 203/20 is 10 3/20 rupees.

mcqs.q: Afzal got 2/5 of a chocolate bar and Fazila got 3/10. By how much did Afzal get more than Fazila?
mcqs.why: Compare with the LCM of 5 and 10, which is 10. Afzal got 2/5 = 4/10 and Fazila got 3/10, and 4/10 is bigger than 3/10, so Afzal got more. Difference: 4/10 - 3/10 = 1/10 of the bar.

mcqs.q: The price of one packet of biscuits is Rs 12 1/2. Find the price of 2 dozen packets.
mcqs.why: First, 2 dozen means 2 x 12 = 24 packets. Change the price: 12 1/2 is 25/2. Total price: 24 x 25/2 = 300, because 24 ÷ 2 = 12 and 12 x 25 = 300 rupees.

mcqs.q: Shumaila buys 2 1/4 m of ribbon and uses 1 7/8 m of it. How much ribbon is left?
mcqs.why: Ribbon left means subtract: 2 1/4 - 1 7/8. Change them into 9/4 and 15/8. With LCM 8: 9/4 = 18/8. Then 18/8 - 15/8 = 3/8. So 3/8 m of ribbon is left.

mcqs.q: 75 3/4 kg of tea is packed into packets of 3/8 kg each. How many packets are needed?
mcqs.why: Number of packets means divide: 75 3/4 ÷ 3/8. Change 75 3/4 into 303/4. Multiply by the reciprocal of 3/8: 303/4 x 8/3 = 2424/12, because 303 x 8 = 2424 and 4 x 3 = 12. Then 2424 ÷ 12 = 202 packets.

mcqs.q: Simplify using BODMAS: 3/4 + 3/4 of 3/4 ÷ 3/4 - (3/4 x 3/4)
Simplify using BODMAS: 2 1/3 - (16/5 ÷ 1 7/8 of 2 2/15) + 1 1/8
What is the reciprocal of 2 1/2?
mcqs.why: First change the mixed number into an improper fraction: 2 1/2 is 5/2, because 2 x 2 = 4 and 4 + 1 = 5. Now turn 5/2 upside down, so the numerator and denominator change places. The reciprocal is 2/5.

mcqs.q: What is 3/4 of a dozen?
mcqs.why: One dozen means 12 things, and of means multiply. So 3/4 x 12 = 9, because 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 3 x 3 = 9. So 3/4 of a dozen is 9.

mcqs.q: How many centimetres are there in 1 1/2 m?
mcqs.why: One metre has 100 centimetres. Change 1 1/2 into 3/2. Then multiply: 3/2 x 100 = 150, because 100 ÷ 2 = 50 and 3 x 50 = 150. So 1 1/2 m is 150 cm.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1 — Addition and Subtraction of Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Adding Decimals

Write the numbers so that the decimal points are exactly below each other. Write 0 in any empty place so both numbers have the same number of decimal places. Then add column by column, just like whole numbers, and put the point in the answer below the other points.

Subtracting Decimals

Use the same lining up. Keep the points in one line, fill empty places with 0, and subtract column by column. Borrow from the next column when the top digit is smaller.

  • 4.567 + 36.4 is written as 4.567 + 36.400.
  • 25.52 - 6.3 is written as 25.52 - 6.30.
  • Always check that the point in the answer sits in the same column as the points above it.

mcqs.why: Line up the points and add column by column: 22.32 + 6.46 = 28.78, because 32 + 46 = 78 hundredths and 22 + 6 = 28.
First write 36.4 as 36.400 so both numbers have three decimal places. Then 4.567 + 36.400 = 40.967.
Add the hundredths first: 5 + 2 = 7, then the tenths: 0 + 6 = 6, then the whole part: 75 + 24 = 99. So 75.05 + 24.62 = 99.67.
Write 0.25 as 0.250 to fill the empty thousandths place. Then 257.003 + 0.250 = 257.253.
Write 6.3 as 6.30 so the places match. Then subtract column by column: 25.52 - 6.30 = 19.22.
Both numbers already have three decimal places, so subtract directly: 74.567 - 33.402 = 41.165.
Subtract the hundredths with borrowing: 46 - 38 = 8 hundredths after borrowing in the tenths column, and 786 - 345 = 441. So 786.46 - 345.38 = 441.08.
Write 935.69 as 935.690 so it has three decimal places like 805.365. Then 935.690 - 805.365 = 130.325.

mcqs.q: To add 4.567 + 36.4 correctly, how should 36.4 be written?
mcqs.why: The points must line up and empty places are filled with 0. The number 36.4 has one decimal place, so it is written as 36.400 to match the three decimal places of 4.567, and its value does not change.
Add column by column with carrying: 75 + 69 = 144 hundredths, which is 1.44, and 45 + 54 + 1 = 100. So 45.75 + 54.69 = 100.44.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2 — Decimal Places and Multiplying by 10, 100, 1000
lessons.notes_html:
Decimal Places

The digits after the decimal point are called decimal places. One digit after the point means one decimal place, two digits mean two places, and three digits mean three places.

  • 0.6 and 62.1 have one decimal place.
  • 0.08, 34.25, 3.36 and 38.66 have two decimal places.
  • 2.123 and 52.302 have three decimal places.

Multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000

When you multiply by 10, the point moves one place to the right. For 100 it moves two places right, and for 1000 it moves three places right. Add a 0 if there are not enough digits.

mcqs.q: How many decimal places does 2.123 have?
mcqs.why: Count the digits after the decimal point. In 2.123 the digits 1, 2 and 3 come after the point, so it has three decimal places.

mcqs.q: Which number has exactly two decimal places?
mcqs.why: The number 34.25 has the two digits 2 and 5 after the point. The numbers 0.6 and 62.1 have one place each, and 52.302 has three places.

mcqs.q: What is 0.175 x 10?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right: 0.175 x 10 = 1.75.

mcqs.q: What is 0.175 x 1000?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 1000 moves the decimal point three places to the right: 0.175 x 1000 = 175.

mcqs.q: What is 35.058 x 100?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right: 35.058 x 100 = 3505.8.

mcqs.q: What is 8.15 x 100?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 100 moves the point two places right, and a 0 fills the last place: 8.15 x 100 = 815.

mcqs.q: What is 324.423 x 10?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right: 324.423 x 10 = 3244.23.
Multiplying by 1000 moves the point three places to the right: 0.0067 x 1000 = 6.7.

mcqs.q: When a decimal is multiplied by 100, the decimal point moves:
mcqs.why: The number 100 has two zeros, so the point moves two places to the right. For example, 8.15 x 100 = 815.

mcqs.q: What is 8.15 x 1000?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 1000 moves the point three places to the right, adding one 0 at the end: 8.15 x 1000 = 8150.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3 — Divide by 10, 100 and 1000
lessons.notes_html:
The Rule for Division

Dividing is the opposite of multiplying. When you divide by 10, the decimal point moves one place to the left. For 100 it moves two places left, and for 1000 it moves three places left.

When Zeros Are Needed

If there are not enough digits on the left, write extra zeros in front of the number. For example, 0.085 divided by 1000 becomes 0.000085.

  • Dividing makes the number smaller.
  • Count the zeros in the divisor: that is how many places the point moves.

mcqs.q: What is 6.675 / 10?
mcqs.why: Dividing by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the left: 6.675 / 10 = 0.6675.
Dividing by 1000 moves the decimal point three places to the left, so a zero is written after the point: 6.675 / 1000 = 0.006675.

mcqs.q: What is 35.89 / 10?
mcqs.why: Dividing by 10 moves the point one place to the left: 35.89 / 10 = 3.589.
Dividing by 100 moves the point two places to the left: 35.89 / 100 = 0.3589.
Dividing by 100 moves the point two places to the left: 815.4 / 100 = 8.154.
Dividing by 1000 moves the point three places to the left: 815.4 / 1000 = 0.8154.

mcqs.q: What is 0.085 / 10?
mcqs.why: Dividing by 10 moves the point one place left, so an extra zero is needed in front: 0.085 / 10 = 0.0085.
Dividing by 1000 moves the point three places left, and zeros fill the empty places: 0.085 / 1000 = 0.000085.

mcqs.q: When a decimal is divided by 1000, the decimal point moves:
mcqs.why: The number 1000 has three zeros, and division moves the point to the left, so it moves three places to the left. For example, 815.4 / 1000 = 0.8154.
Dividing by 1000 moves the point three places to the left, with a zero filling the gap: 35.89 / 1000 = 0.03589.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4 — Multiply a Decimal by a Whole Number
lessons.notes_html:
The Method

First multiply the numbers without the decimal point, as if they were whole numbers. Then count the decimal places in the given decimal number. Finally, count the same number of places from the right in the answer and put the decimal point there.

  • 6.5 x 5: 65 x 5 = 325, and 6.5 has one decimal place, so the answer is 32.5.
  • 0.382 x 5: 382 x 5 = 1910, and 0.382 has three decimal places, so the answer is 1.910, written as 1.91.
  • A zero at the very end after the point can be dropped.

mcqs.q: What is 6.5 x 5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 65 x 5 = 325. The number 6.5 has one decimal place, so place the point one place from the right: 6.5 x 5 = 32.5.

mcqs.q: What is 0.65 x 5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 65 x 5 = 325. The number 0.65 has two decimal places, so the answer has two places: 0.65 x 5 = 3.25.

mcqs.q: What is 0.35 x 8?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 35 x 8 = 280. The number 0.35 has two decimal places, so count two places from the right: 0.35 x 8 = 2.8.

mcqs.q: What is 4.25 x 7?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 425 x 7 = 2975. The number 4.25 has two decimal places, so 4.25 x 7 = 29.75.

mcqs.q: What is 4.25 x 9?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 425 x 9 = 3825. The number 4.25 has two decimal places, so 4.25 x 9 = 38.25.

mcqs.q: What is 0.382 x 5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 382 x 5 = 1910. The number 0.382 has three decimal places, so count three places from the right: 0.382 x 5 = 1.91.

mcqs.q: What is 24.58 x 7?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 2458 x 7 = 17206. The number 24.58 has two decimal places, so 24.58 x 7 = 172.06.

mcqs.q: What is 0.265 x 36?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 265 x 36 = 9540. The number 0.265 has three decimal places, so count three places from the right: 0.265 x 36 = 9.54.

mcqs.q: What is 4.25 x 27?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 425 x 27 = 11475. The number 4.25 has two decimal places, so 4.25 x 27 = 114.75.

mcqs.q: What is 0.394 x 8?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the point: 394 x 8 = 3152. The number 0.394 has three decimal places, so count three places from the right: 0.394 x 8 = 3.152.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5 — Divide a Decimal by a Whole Number
lessons.notes_html:
The Method

Divide in the ordinary way, digit by digit. When you reach the decimal point in the number being divided, put a point in the answer at the same place, then keep dividing.

  • If the first digit is smaller than the divisor, write 0 in the answer and continue.
  • Add a 0 after the point and keep going if there is a remainder.
  • When the answer is asked up to 3 decimal places, work one more place and round the third place up if the next digit is 5 or more.

mcqs.q: What is 0.65 / 5?
mcqs.why: Divide 65 by 5 to get 13, and the point in 0.65 is two places from the right, so 0.65 / 5 = 0.13. Check: 0.13 x 5 = 0.65.

mcqs.q: What is 6.5 / 5?
mcqs.why: Divide digit by digit and put the point in the answer when you pass the point in 6.5: 6.5 / 5 = 1.3. Check: 1.3 x 5 = 6.5.

mcqs.q: What is 3.6 / 6?
mcqs.why: The whole part 3 is smaller than 6, so write 0 and divide 36 tenths by 6 to get 6 tenths: 3.6 / 6 = 0.6. Check: 0.6 x 6 = 3.6.

mcqs.q: What is 4.27 / 7?
mcqs.why: Divide 42 tenths by 7 to get 6 tenths, then 7 hundredths by 7 to get 1 hundredth: 4.27 / 7 = 0.61. Check: 0.61 x 7 = 4.27.

mcqs.q: What is 9.6 / 8?
mcqs.why: Divide 9 by 8 to get 1 with remainder 1, then divide 16 tenths by 8 to get 2 tenths: 9.6 / 8 = 1.2. Check: 1.2 x 8 = 9.6.

mcqs.q: What is 44.1 / 9?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 9 x 4 = 36 leaves 8, bring down the 1 tenth to make 81 tenths, and 81 / 9 = 9 tenths. So 44.1 / 9 = 4.9. Check: 4.9 x 9 = 44.1.

mcqs.q: What is 0.385 / 5?
mcqs.why: Divide 385 thousandths by 5 to get 77 thousandths: 0.385 / 5 = 0.077. Check: 0.077 x 5 = 0.385.

mcqs.q: What is 8.394 / 6?
mcqs.why: Divide digit by digit, keeping the point in line: the answer builds up as 1, then 1.3, then 1.39, then 1.399. So 8.394 / 6 = 1.399. Check: 1.399 x 6 = 8.394.

mcqs.q: What is 87.03 / 9?
mcqs.why: Divide digit by digit: 9 x 9 = 81 leaves 6.03, and 603 hundredths divided by 9 gives 67 hundredths, which is 0.67. So 87.03 / 9 = 9.67. Check: 9.67 x 9 = 87.03.

mcqs.q: What is 40.25 / 4 up to 3 decimal places, correctly rounded?
mcqs.why: Full working: 40.25 / 4 = 10.0625. The fourth decimal digit is 5, so the third place rounds up from 2 to 3, giving 10.063. Note: the solved book prints 10.062 because it simply drops the extra digit instead of rounding; the correctly rounded answer is 10.063.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.6 — Multiply by Tenths and Hundredths
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplying by 0.1, 0.2, 0.01 and So On

Multiply the numbers without the points. Then count the total decimal places in both numbers together, and count that many places from the right in the answer to place the point.

  • 2.6 x 0.1: 26 x 1 = 26, and the total is two places, so the answer is 0.26.
  • 0.01 x 0.01: 1 x 1 = 1, and the total is four places, so the answer is 0.0001.
  • Write zeros in front when the answer does not have enough digits.

mcqs.q: What is 2.6 x 0.1?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 26 x 1 = 26. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so count two places from the right: 2.6 x 0.1 = 0.26.

mcqs.q: What is 3.87 x 0.2?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 387 x 2 = 774. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 3.87 x 0.2 = 0.774.

mcqs.q: What is 42.5 x 0.3?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 425 x 3 = 1275. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 42.5 x 0.3 = 12.75.

mcqs.q: What is 0.3 x 0.5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 3 x 5 = 15. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 0.3 x 0.5 = 0.15.

mcqs.q: What is 0.01 x 0.6?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 1 x 6 = 6. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so a zero fills the gap: 0.01 x 0.6 = 0.006.

mcqs.q: What is 1.1 x 0.4?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 11 x 4 = 44. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 1.1 x 0.4 = 0.44.

mcqs.q: What is 2.6 x 0.03?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 26 x 3 = 78. Total decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3, so 2.6 x 0.03 = 0.078.

mcqs.q: What is 0.01 x 0.01?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 1 x 1 = 1. Total decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4, so zeros fill the front places: 0.01 x 0.01 = 0.0001.

mcqs.q: What is 42.5 x 0.05?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 425 x 5 = 2125. Total decimal places: 1 + 2 = 3, so 42.5 x 0.05 = 2.125.

mcqs.q: What is 59.95 x 0.07?
