mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 5995 x 7 = 41965. Total decimal places: 2 + 2 = 4, so 59.95 x 0.07 = 4.1965.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.7 — Multiply a Decimal by a Decimal
lessons.notes_html:
The General Rule

Multiply the two numbers without the points, as whole numbers. Then add the decimal places of both numbers. Count that total from the right in the answer and place the decimal point.

  • 46.7 x 1.2: the whole-number product is 5604, and 1 + 1 = 2 places, so the answer is 56.04.
  • 0.065 x 0.25: the product is 1625, and 3 + 2 = 5 places, so the answer is 0.01625.
  • If the answer has fewer digits than the places needed, write zeros in front.

mcqs.q: Multiplying 46.7 x 1.2 without the points gives 5604. What is the correct answer with the point placed?
mcqs.why: Count the places in both numbers: 46.7 has 1 place and 1.2 has 1 place, total 2 places. Counting two places from the right in 5604 gives 46.7 x 1.2 = 56.04.

mcqs.q: What is 3.57 x 1.2?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 357 x 12 = 4284. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 3.57 x 1.2 = 4.284.

mcqs.q: What is 0.28 x 0.4?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 28 x 4 = 112. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 0.28 x 0.4 = 0.112.

mcqs.q: What is 0.45 x 0.5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 45 x 5 = 225. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 0.45 x 0.5 = 0.225.

mcqs.q: What is 0.2 x 0.023?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 2 x 23 = 46. Total decimal places: 1 + 3 = 4, so zeros fill the front: 0.2 x 0.023 = 0.0046.

mcqs.q: What is 1.4 x 2.5?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 14 x 25 = 350. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 1.4 x 2.5 = 3.5.

mcqs.q: What is 3.8 x 0.7?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 38 x 7 = 266. Total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2, so 3.8 x 0.7 = 2.66.

mcqs.q: What is 4.45 x 1.8?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 445 x 18 = 8010. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 4.45 x 1.8 = 8.01.

mcqs.q: What is 5.25 x 4.4?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 525 x 44 = 23100. Total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3, so 5.25 x 4.4 = 23.1.

mcqs.q: What is 0.065 x 0.25?
mcqs.why: Multiply without the points: 65 x 25 = 1625. Total decimal places: 3 + 2 = 5, so a zero is written in front: 0.065 x 0.25 = 0.01625.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.8 — Divide a Decimal by a Decimal
lessons.notes_html:
Making the Divisor a Whole Number

Move the decimal point in the divisor until it becomes a whole number. Move the point in the other number by the same number of places. Then divide in the ordinary way.

  • 2.16 / 0.6 becomes 21.6 / 6, and the answer is 3.6.
  • 0.016 / 0.2 becomes 0.16 / 2, and the answer is 0.08.

Using Fractions

You can also change both numbers into fractions and divide. For example, 5.76 / 0.24 becomes 576 / 24, and the answer is 24. Both methods give the same answer.

mcqs.q: What is 2.16 / 0.6?
mcqs.why: Move the point one place in both numbers: 2.16 / 0.6 = 21.6 / 6. Then 21.6 / 6 = 3.6. Check: 3.6 x 0.6 = 2.16.
Move the point two places in both numbers: 5.76 / 0.24 = 576 / 24. Then 576 / 24 = 24. Check: 24 x 0.24 = 5.76.

mcqs.q: What is 4.41 / 0.3?
mcqs.why: Move the point one place in both numbers: 4.41 / 0.3 = 44.1 / 3. Then 44.1 / 3 = 14.7. Check: 14.7 x 0.3 = 4.41.
Move the point two places in both numbers: 7.84 / 0.07 = 784 / 7. Then 784 / 7 = 112. Check: 112 x 0.07 = 7.84.
Move the point one place in both numbers: 0.016 / 0.2 = 0.16 / 2. Then 0.16 / 2 = 0.08. Check: 0.08 x 0.2 = 0.016.

mcqs.q: What is 0.36 / 0.6?
mcqs.why: Move the point one place in both numbers: 0.36 / 0.6 = 3.6 / 6. Then 3.6 / 6 = 0.6. Check: 0.6 x 0.6 = 0.36.

mcqs.q: What is 0.96 / 0.4?
mcqs.why: Move the point one place in both numbers: 0.96 / 0.4 = 9.6 / 4. Then 9.6 / 4 = 2.4. Check: 2.4 x 0.4 = 0.96.
Move the point one place in both numbers: 9.018 / 0.9 = 90.18 / 9. Then 90.18 / 9 = 10.02. Check: 10.02 x 0.9 = 9.018.
Move the point two places in both numbers: 0.325 / 0.25 = 32.5 / 25. Then 32.5 / 25 = 1.3. Check: 1.3 x 0.25 = 0.325.
Move the point two places in both numbers: 10.24 / 0.08 = 1024 / 8. Then 1024 / 8 = 128. Check: 128 x 0.08 = 10.24.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.9 — Change Fractions into Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
How to Change a Fraction into a Decimal

To change a fraction into a decimal, divide the numerator (top number) by the denominator (bottom number).

Steps

  • Divide the top number by the bottom number.
  • Keep dividing after the decimal point until the division ends or the pattern repeats.
  • Like the book, stop the answer at 3 decimal places when the division does not end.

Examples

5 / 4 = 1.25 and 5 / 8 = 0.625. These divisions end, so the decimals are exact. The division 5 / 3 gives 1.6666 and the digits keep repeating, so we stop at 3 decimal places and write 1.666.

mcqs.q: Change 5/4 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide the numerator by the denominator. 5 / 4 = 1.25. Check: 1.25 x 4 = 5, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Change 4/5 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 10 first. 4 / 5 = 8 / 10 = 0.8. So 4/5 changed into a decimal is 0.8.

mcqs.q: Change 5/8 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 5 by 8 step by step. 5 / 8 = 0.625. Check: 0.625 x 8 = 5, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Change 7/10 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: a denominator of 10 means one decimal place. 7 / 10 = 0.7. So 7/10 changed into a decimal is 0.7.

mcqs.q: Change 15/7 into a decimal, stopping at 3 decimal places.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 15 by 7. The division gives 2.142857 and the digits keep going, so stopping at 3 decimal places the answer is 2.142, as the book does.

mcqs.q: Change 23/25 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 100 first. 23 / 25 = 92 / 100 = 0.92. So 23/25 changed into a decimal is 0.92.

mcqs.q: Change 250/8 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 250 by 8. 250 / 8 = 31.25. Check: 31.25 x 8 = 250, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Change 11/16 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 11 by 16 step by step. 11 / 16 = 0.6875. Check: 0.6875 x 16 = 11, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Change 300/250 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: cancel the fraction first, then divide. 300 / 250 = 30 / 25 = 1.2. So 300/250 changed into a decimal is 1.2.

mcqs.q: Change 17/20 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 100 first. 17 / 20 = 85 / 100 = 0.85. So 17/20 changed into a decimal is 0.85.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.10 — Simplify Decimal Expressions with Brackets
lessons.notes_html:
The BODMAS Rule

When an expression has brackets, follow BODMAS: Brackets first, then Division and Multiplication, then Addition and Subtraction.

Steps

  • Solve the part inside the brackets first. If there are brackets inside brackets, solve the innermost one first.
  • Then do multiplication and division from left to right.
  • Then do addition and subtraction from left to right.
  • Line up the decimal points carefully in every step.

Example

For 5.6 + 7.22 - (2.24 + 4.68), the bracket gives 2.24 + 4.68 = 6.92, and then 5.6 + 7.22 - 6.92 = 5.9.

mcqs.why: Working: do the multiplication in the bracket first. 20.14 x 5.6 = 112.784. Then 112.784 + 10.9335 = 123.7175.
Working: bracket first, from left to right. 23.35 - 8.30 + 8.34 = 23.39. Then 4.6 + 6.07 + 23.39 = 34.06.
Working: bracket first. 1.84 + 3.29 = 5.13. Then work from left to right. 14.3 - 2.8 + 5.13 = 16.63.
Working: brackets first. 25.5 - 12.2 = 13.3 and 2.3 + 2.6 = 4.9. Then multiply. 5.6 x 13.3 = 74.48. Then 74.48 + 4.9 = 79.38.
Working: bracket and multiplication first. 3.45 x 8.56 = 29.532 and 2.2 - 1.12 = 1.08. Then 29.532 - 4.23 + 1.08 = 26.382.
Working: brackets first. 6.6 x 3.59 = 23.694 and 1.12 + 0.1 = 1.22. Then work from left to right. 23.694 - 1.22 - 1.02 = 21.454.
Working: brackets first. 5.24 + 2.02 = 7.26 and 9.405 - 2.24 = 7.165. Then work from left to right. 7.26 - 0.96 - 7.45 + 7.165 = 6.015.

mcqs.q: In 4.6 + 6.07 + (23.35 - 8.30 + 8.34), which part must be solved first?
mcqs.why: By the BODMAS rule, brackets are always solved before addition and subtraction outside them, so the part inside the brackets is worked out first.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.11 — Round off Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
What Rounding Off Means

Rounding off means writing a decimal as a nearer, simpler number. Look at the digit just after the place you are rounding to.

The Rule

  • If that digit is 5 or more, round up: increase the last kept digit by 1.
  • If that digit is less than 5, round down: keep the last kept digit the same.

Places

  • To round to a whole number, look at the tenths digit.
  • To round to one decimal place, look at the hundredths digit.
  • To round to two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit.

For example, in 5.95 the hundredths digit is 5, so rounding to one decimal place gives 6.0.

mcqs.q: Round off 5.6 as a whole number.
mcqs.why: The tenths digit in 5.6 is 6, which is 5 or more, so we round up and the whole number becomes 6.

mcqs.q: Round off 50.2 as a whole number.
mcqs.why: The tenths digit in 50.2 is 2, which is less than 5, so we keep the whole part the same and the answer is 50.

mcqs.q: Round off 99.9 as a whole number.
mcqs.why: The tenths digit in 99.9 is 9, which is 5 or more, so 99 rounds up by one whole and the answer becomes 100.

mcqs.q: Round off 32.38 up to one decimal place.
mcqs.why: For one decimal place, look at the hundredths digit. In 32.38 it is 8, which is 5 or more, so the tenths digit 3 becomes 4 and the answer is 32.4.

mcqs.q: Round off 5.95 up to one decimal place.
mcqs.why: For one decimal place, look at the hundredths digit. In 5.95 it is 5, so we round up: the tenths digit 9 becomes 10, and the answer is written as 6.0.

mcqs.q: Round off 3.432 up to one decimal place.
mcqs.why: For one decimal place, look at the hundredths digit. In 3.432 it is 3, which is less than 5, so the tenths digit stays 4 and the answer is 3.4.

mcqs.q: Round off 32.386 up to two decimal places.
mcqs.why: For two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. In 32.386 it is 6, which is 5 or more, so the hundredths digit 8 becomes 9 and the answer is 32.39.

mcqs.q: Round off 6.775 up to two decimal places.
mcqs.why: For two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. In 6.775 it is 5, so we round up: the hundredths digit 7 becomes 8 and the answer is 6.78.

mcqs.q: Round off 0.9627 up to two decimal places.
mcqs.why: For two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. In 0.9627 it is 2, which is less than 5, so the hundredths digit stays 6 and the answer is 0.96.

mcqs.q: Round off 4.0098 up to two decimal places.
mcqs.why: For two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. In 4.0098 it is 9, which is 5 or more, so the hundredths digit 0 becomes 1 and the answer is 4.01.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.12 — Convert Fractions and Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Fraction into Decimal

Divide the numerator by the denominator, or make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000 and then place the decimal point. For example, 17 / 25 = 68 / 100 = 0.68.

Decimal into Fraction

  • Count the decimal places in the number.
  • Write the number without the point over 10, 100, 1000 and so on, with the same count of zeros.
  • Cancel common factors to write the fraction in its lowest form.

Example

The decimal 0.25 has two decimal places: 0.25 = 25 / 100 = 1 / 4 in lowest form.

mcqs.q: Convert 7/8 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide the numerator by the denominator. 7 / 8 = 0.875. Check: 0.875 x 8 = 7, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Convert 17/25 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 100 first. 17 / 25 = 68 / 100 = 0.68. So 17/25 converted into a decimal is 0.68.

mcqs.q: Convert 61/50 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide 61 by 50. 61 / 50 = 1.22. Check: 1.22 x 50 = 61, so the answer is correct.

mcqs.q: Convert 451/500 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 1000 first. 451 / 500 = 902 / 1000 = 0.902. So 451/500 converted into a decimal is 0.902.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.5 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: one decimal place means tenths. 0.5 = 5 / 10 = 1 / 2 after cancelling the common factor 5 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.25 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: two decimal places mean hundredths. 0.25 = 25 / 100 = 1 / 4 after cancelling the common factor 25 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 1.05 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: two decimal places mean hundredths. 1.05 = 105 / 100 = 21 / 20 after cancelling the common factor 5 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.064 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: three decimal places mean thousandths. 0.064 = 64 / 1000 = 8 / 125 after cancelling the common factor 8 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 41.625 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: three decimal places mean thousandths. 41.625 = 41625 / 1000 = 333 / 8 after cancelling the common factor 125 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 79/250 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: make the denominator 1000 first. 79 / 250 = 316 / 1000 = 0.316. So 79/250 converted into a decimal is 0.316.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.13 — Word Problems on Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Solving Word Problems

Read the problem carefully and decide which operation to use.

  • Total or altogether usually means add.
  • How much more, left or remaining usually means subtract.
  • The same amount repeated many times means multiply.
  • Sharing or finding the price or amount for one item means divide.

Careful Points

  • Line up the decimal points when you add or subtract.
  • Write the unit, such as kg, m or Rs, with the final answer.
  • April has 30 days, and one month is often taken as 30 days in these problems.

mcqs.q: Sahir bought two chickens of weight 1.450 kg and 1.685 kg. What is the total weight of both chickens?
mcqs.why: Working: total means add, lining up the decimal points. 1.450 + 1.685 = 3.135. So the total weight of both chickens is 3.135 kg.

mcqs.q: A store sold 200.750 kg of flour and 98.500 kg of sugar. How much more flour was sold than sugar?
mcqs.why: Working: how much more means subtract the smaller amount from the bigger one. 200.750 - 98.500 = 102.25. So 102.25 kg more flour was sold.

mcqs.q: Saira bought a necklace of mass 2.565 g and bangles of mass 8.875 g. What is the total mass of the two items?
mcqs.why: Working: total means add, lining up the decimal points. 2.565 + 8.875 = 11.44. So the total mass of the two items is 11.44 g.

mcqs.q: Aftab saved Rs 3,206.75 from a monthly salary of Rs 35,200. Find his monthly expenditure.
mcqs.why: Working: expenditure is salary minus savings. 35200 - 3206.75 = 31993.25. So Aftab spends Rs 31,993.25 in the month.

mcqs.q: A shop earns Rs 2,345.75 in one day by selling easy load balance. How much will it earn in one month of 30 days?
mcqs.why: Working: the same amount for 30 days means multiply by 30. 2345.75 x 30 = 70372.5. So the shop will earn Rs 70,372.50 in one month.

mcqs.q: A bundle contains 119.5 m of wire. A piece of 29.92 m is sold. Find the length of the remaining wire.
mcqs.why: Working: remaining means subtract the sold piece from the full bundle. 119.5 - 29.92 = 89.58. So the length of the remaining wire is 89.58 m.

mcqs.q: The height of a pole is 18.75 m. A ladder is 1/3 of the pole. How much of the pole is left above the ladder?
mcqs.why: Working: first find the ladder length. 18.75 x 1 / 3 = 6.25. Then subtract from the pole. 18.75 - 6.25 = 12.5. So 12.5 m of the pole is left above the ladder.

mcqs.q: One school uniform is made from 4.5 m of cloth. How many uniforms can be made from 31.5 m of cloth?
mcqs.why: Working: divide the total cloth by the cloth for one uniform. 31.5 / 4.5 = 315 / 45 = 7. So 7 uniforms can be made from 31.5 m of cloth.

mcqs.q: A lady used 3.60 kg of salt in the month of April, which has 30 days. How much salt is used per day?
mcqs.why: Working: per day means divide the total salt by the number of days in April. 3.60 / 30 = 0.12. So 0.12 kg of salt is used per day.

mcqs.q: The price of 2.5 kg of ghee is Rs 391.25. Find the price of 1 kg of ghee.
mcqs.why: Working: the price of 1 kg means divide the total price by the weight. 391.25 / 2.5 = 156.5. So the price of 1 kg of ghee is Rs 156.50.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.14 — Percentage, Fraction and Decimal
lessons.notes_html:
What Percentage Means

Percentage means out of 100. The sign for percentage is %.

Changing Forms

  • Percentage into fraction: write the number over 100 and cancel to lowest form.
  • Percentage into decimal: divide the number by 100, which moves the point two places to the left.
  • Decimal into percentage: multiply by 100, which moves the point two places to the right, and write the % sign.
  • Fraction into percentage: multiply the fraction by 100 and write the % sign.

Examples

25% = 25 / 100 = 1 / 4 and 25 / 100 = 0.25. Also 5 / 8 x 100 = 62.5, so 5/8 is 62.5%.

mcqs.q: Convert 25% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: percentage means out of 100. 25% = 25 / 100 = 1 / 4 after cancelling the common factor 25 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 65% into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide the percentage number by 100. 65% = 65 / 100 = 0.65. So 65% converted into a decimal is 0.65.

mcqs.q: Convert 85% into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: percentage means out of 100. 85% = 85 / 100 = 17 / 20 after cancelling the common factor 5 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 105% into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide the percentage number by 100. 105% = 105 / 100 = 1.05. A percentage greater than 100 gives a decimal greater than 1.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.8 into a percentage.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the decimal by 100 and write the % sign. 0.8 x 100 = 80. So the decimal 0.8 is the same as 80%.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.34 into a fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Working: two decimal places mean hundredths. 0.34 = 34 / 100 = 17 / 50 after cancelling the common factor 2 from the top and bottom.

mcqs.q: Convert 3.45 into a percentage.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the decimal by 100 and write the % sign. 3.45 x 100 = 345. So the decimal 3.45 is the same as 345%.

mcqs.q: Express 5/8 as a percentage.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the fraction by 100. 5 / 8 x 100 = 62.5. So the fraction 5/8 expressed as a percentage is 62.5%.

mcqs.q: Express 17/40 as a percentage.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the fraction by 100. 17 / 40 x 100 = 42.5. So the fraction 17/40 expressed as a percentage is 42.5%.

mcqs.q: Express 71/50 as a percentage.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the fraction by 100. 71 / 50 x 100 = 142. So the fraction 71/50 expressed as a percentage is 142%.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.15 — Word Problems on Percentages
lessons.notes_html:
Finding a Percentage of a Number

To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100.

Steps

  • Write the percentage as a fraction over 100.
  • Multiply it by the given number.
  • Cancel zeros where you can, then divide to get the answer.

Discount Problems

  • First find the discount: the percentage of the original price.
  • Then subtract the discount from the original price to get the sale price.

Example

20 / 100 of 450 cars: 450 x 20 / 100 = 90, so 20% of 450 is 90.

mcqs.q: 480 students visited a book fair. 45% of them are boys. How many boys visited the book fair?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 480 x 45 / 100 = 216. So 216 boys visited the book fair.

mcqs.q: 825 students are studying in a school. 60% of them were regular for the whole session. How many students were regular?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 825 x 60 / 100 = 495. So 495 students were regular for the whole session.

mcqs.q: 900 employees work in a company. 70% of them use English frequently. How many employees use English frequently?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 900 x 70 / 100 = 630. So 630 employees use English frequently.

mcqs.q: There are 2,400 houses in a colony and 65% of them have computers. How many houses have computers?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 2400 x 65 / 100 = 1560. So 1,560 houses in the colony have computers.

mcqs.q: A school has 1,200 students in total. Class V has 20% of the students. How many students are in Class V?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 1200 x 20 / 100 = 240. So there are 240 students in Class V.

mcqs.q: There are 450 cars in a car parking and 20% of them are white. How many cars are white?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 450 x 20 / 100 = 90. So 90 cars in the parking are white in colour.

mcqs.q: The original price of a dress is Rs 1,650. It is sold at a 9% discount. What is the sale price of the dress?
mcqs.why: Working: first find the discount. 1650 x 9 / 100 = 148.5. Then subtract it from the price. 1650 - 148.5 = 1501.5. So the sale price is Rs 1,501.50.

mcqs.q: A town has 600 trees and 35% of them are mango trees. How many mango trees are there?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 600 x 35 / 100 = 210. So there are 210 mango trees in the town.

mcqs.q: A basket has 200 oranges and 15% of them are rotten. How many oranges are rotten?
mcqs.why: Working: multiply the total by the percentage over 100. 200 x 15 / 100 = 30. So 30 oranges in the basket are rotten.

mcqs.q: A shirt costs Rs 800. It is sold at a 10% discount. What is the sale price of the shirt?
mcqs.why: Working: first find the discount. 800 x 10 / 100 = 80. Then subtract it from the price. 800 - 80 = 720. So the sale price of the shirt is Rs 720.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 4
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 4

This review mixes all the skills of the unit: moving the decimal point, changing between fractions, decimals and percentages, rounding, ordering and word problems.

Key Points

  • Multiplying by 100 moves the point two places to the right; dividing by 100 moves it two places to the left.
  • 65% = 65 / 100 = 0.65.
  • To compare decimals, compare the whole parts first, then tenths, then hundredths.
  • To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage over 100.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 42.0 divided by ____ gives 0.42.
mcqs.why: Working: the point in 42.0 moved two places to the left to make 0.42, and moving two places left means dividing by 100. Check: 42.0 / 100 = 0.42.

mcqs.q: Fill in the blank: 12.04 multiplied by ____ gives 1204.
mcqs.why: Working: the point in 12.04 moved two places to the right to make 1204, and moving two places right means multiplying by 100. Check: 12.04 x 100 = 1204.

mcqs.q: Write 65% as a decimal.
mcqs.why: Working: divide the percentage number by 100. 65% = 65 / 100 = 0.65. So 65% written as a decimal is 0.65.
Working: add place by place, lining up the decimal points. 4 + 0.4 + 0.04 + 0.004 = 4.444. Each part fills the next decimal place.

mcqs.q: Round off 4.956 to two decimal places.
mcqs.why: For two decimal places, look at the thousandths digit. In 4.956 it is 6, which is 5 or more, so the hundredths digit 5 becomes 6 and the answer is 4.96.

mcqs.q: Arrange in ascending order: 0.016, 2.087, 1.995, 0.463
mcqs.why: Working: ascending means smallest first. Compare whole parts first: the two numbers starting with 0 come before 1.995 and 2.087, and 0.016 is smaller than 0.463 because its tenths digit is smaller.
Working: work from left to right, lining up the decimal points. 9.123 - 5.865 = 3.258. Then 3.258 + 2.403 = 5.661.

mcqs.q: The height of an electric pole is 14.95 m and the height of a mobile tower is 25.04 m. How much higher is the mobile tower than the electric pole?
mcqs.why: Working: how much higher means subtract the smaller height from the bigger height. 25.04 - 14.95 = 10.09. So the mobile tower is 10.09 m higher.

mcqs.q: Divide 0.72 by 1.2.
mcqs.why: Working: multiply both numbers by 10 to make the divisor whole. 0.72 / 1.2 = 7.2 / 12 = 0.6. So the answer of the division is 0.6.

mcqs.q: 3.6 m of cloth is required to make one dress. How many dresses can be prepared from 14.4 m of cloth?
mcqs.why: Working: divide the total cloth by the cloth needed for one dress. 14.4 / 3.6 = 144 / 36 = 4. So 4 dresses can be prepared from 14.4 m of cloth.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1 — Convert Units of Length
lessons.notes_html:
Length units

The big unit for distance is the kilometre (km). Then come the metre (m), the centimetre (cm) and the millimetre (mm).

Conversion facts

  • 1 km = 1000 m
  • 1 m = 100 cm
  • 1 cm = 10 mm
  • 1 m = 1000 mm

Big unit to small unit

Multiply. For example, 8 x 1000 = 8000, so 8 km is 8000 m. For a mixed length, change the big part first and then add the small part: 20 x 1000 = 20000 and 20000 + 340 = 20340, so 20 km 340 m is 20340 m.

Small unit to big unit

Divide. Dividing metres by 1000 gives kilometres and the metres left over. Dividing centimetres by 100 gives metres and the centimetres left over. Dividing millimetres by 10 gives centimetres and the millimetres left over.

mcqs.q: How many kilometres and metres are there in 1600 m?
mcqs.why: Divide by 1000: 1 x 1000 = 1000 and 1600 - 1000 = 600, so 1600 m is 1 km and the 600 m left over.

mcqs.q: Convert 750 cm into metres and centimetres.
mcqs.why: 100 cm make 1 m. 7 x 100 = 700 and 750 - 700 = 50, so 750 cm is 7 m and 50 cm left over.

mcqs.q: Convert 35 mm into centimetres and millimetres.
mcqs.why: 10 mm make 1 cm. 3 x 10 = 30 and 35 - 30 = 5, so 35 mm is 3 cm and 5 mm left over.

mcqs.q: Convert 899 mm into centimetres and millimetres.
mcqs.why: 10 mm make 1 cm. 89 x 10 = 890 and 899 - 890 = 9, so 899 mm is 89 cm and 9 mm left over.

mcqs.q: Convert 8 km into metres.
mcqs.why: 1 km is 1000 m, so multiply: 8 x 1000 = 8000. Therefore 8 km is 8000 m.

mcqs.q: Convert 20 km 340 m into metres.
mcqs.why: Change the kilometres first: 20 x 1000 = 20000. Then add the metres: 20000 + 340 = 20340, so the total is 20340 m.

mcqs.q: Convert 25 m 45 cm into centimetres.
mcqs.why: 25 x 100 = 2500 gives the centimetres in 25 m. Then 2500 + 45 = 2545, so 25 m 45 cm is 2545 cm.

mcqs.q: Convert 3785 m into kilometres and metres.
How many metres are there in 5000 cm?
mcqs.why: Divide centimetres by 100 to get metres: 5000 / 100 = 50, so 5000 cm is exactly 50 m.

mcqs.q: Convert 4725 mm into centimetres and millimetres.
mcqs.why: 10 mm make 1 cm. 472 x 10 = 4720 and 4725 - 4720 = 5, so 4725 mm is 472 cm and 5 mm.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2 — Add and Subtract Distances
lessons.notes_html:
Adding distances

Write each unit in its own column and add column by column. If the small unit goes past its limit, carry 1 big unit forward.

  • 1000 m or more: carry 1 km.
  • 100 cm or more: carry 1 m.
  • 10 mm or more: carry 1 cm.

Subtracting distances

Subtract column by column. If the top small unit is too small, borrow 1 big unit from the column on its left.

  • Borrow 1 km and it becomes 1000 m.
  • Borrow 1 m and it becomes 100 cm.
  • Borrow 1 cm and it becomes 10 mm.

Example of borrowing: 75 + 1000 = 1075, so 12 km 75 m can be written as 11 km 1075 m before subtracting.

mcqs.q: Add: 43 km 15 m + 66 km 57 m
mcqs.why: Add the columns: 43 + 66 = 109 kilometres and 15 + 57 = 72 metres. Nothing crosses 1000, so the answer is 109 km 72 m.

mcqs.q: Add: 8 m 70 cm + 5 m 60 cm
mcqs.why: 70 + 60 = 130 cm, and 130 cm is 1 m 30 cm because 130 - 100 = 30. Add the metres: 8 + 5 = 13, then 13 + 1 = 14, giving 14 m 30 cm.

mcqs.q: Add: 3 km 918 m + 1 km 324 m
mcqs.why: 918 + 324 = 1242 metres, which is 1 km 242 m because 1242 - 1000 = 242. Kilometres: 3 + 1 = 4, then 4 + 1 = 5, giving 5 km 242 m.

mcqs.q: Add: 45 cm 8 mm + 65 cm 7 mm
mcqs.why: 8 + 7 = 15 mm, which is 1 cm 5 mm because 15 - 10 = 5. Centimetres: 45 + 65 = 110, then 110 + 1 = 111, giving 111 cm 5 mm.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 12 km 75 m - 3 km 84 m
mcqs.why: 75 m is too small, so borrow 1 km: the top becomes 11 km 1075 m because 75 + 1000 = 1075. Then 1075 - 84 = 991 and 11 - 3 = 8, giving 8 km 991 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 51 cm 3 mm - 27 cm 8 mm
mcqs.why: 3 mm is too small, so borrow 1 cm: the top becomes 50 cm 13 mm because 3 + 10 = 13. Then 13 - 8 = 5 and 50 - 27 = 23, giving 23 cm 5 mm.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 5 km 150 m - 2 km 730 m
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km: the top becomes 4 km 1150 m because 150 + 1000 = 1150. Then 1150 - 730 = 420 and 4 - 2 = 2, giving 2 km 420 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 71 m 22 cm - 48 m 85 cm
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m: the top becomes 70 m 122 cm because 22 + 100 = 122. Then 122 - 85 = 37 and 70 - 48 = 22, giving 22 m 37 cm.

mcqs.q: Add: 9 m 58 cm + 4 m 64 cm
mcqs.why: 58 + 64 = 122 cm, which is 1 m 22 cm because 122 - 100 = 22. Metres: 9 + 4 = 13, then 13 + 1 = 14, giving 14 m 22 cm.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 23 cm 2 mm - 17 cm 9 mm
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 cm: the top becomes 22 cm 12 mm because 2 + 10 = 12. Then 12 - 9 = 3 and 22 - 17 = 5, giving 5 cm 3 mm.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3 — Word Problems on Distance
lessons.notes_html:
Reading a word problem

First decide what the question asks. Total distance or length altogether means add. Left, remaining, space left, how much farther or how far ahead means subtract.

Method

  • Keep the same units together: metres with metres, centimetres with centimetres.
  • Carry when the small unit passes 100 cm or 1000 m.
  • Borrow 1 m (100 cm) or 1 km (1000 m) when the top small unit is too small.
  • To compare two distances, subtract the smaller distance from the bigger distance.

Example: 589 + 868 = 1457, so two walks of 589 m and 868 m make a total of 1457 m.

mcqs.q: The length of a ribbon is 6 m 80 cm. How much ribbon is left if 2 m 88 cm has been cut off?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m: 6 m 80 cm becomes 5 m 180 cm because 80 + 100 = 180. Then 180 - 88 = 92 and 5 - 2 = 3, so 3 m 92 cm of ribbon is left.

mcqs.q: Jameel covered 589 m from his house to Jamia Masjid and then 868 m from Jamia Masjid to school. Find the total distance covered by him.
mcqs.why: Add the two parts of the journey: 589 + 868 = 1457, so Jameel covered a total distance of 1457 m.

mcqs.q: A car is 1 m 62 cm wide. A garage is 2 m 41 cm wide. How much space is left when the car is in the garage?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m: 2 m 41 cm becomes 1 m 141 cm because 41 + 100 = 141. Then 141 - 62 = 79, so 79 cm of space is left in the garage.

mcqs.q: Maria's home is 375 m from the school. The railway station is 504 m from her home. Which is farther from her home and by how much?
mcqs.why: Compare the two distances: 504 - 375 = 129, so the railway station is farther from her home by 129 m.

mcqs.q: The red part of a colour pencil is 65 mm long. The blue part is 57 mm long. What is the total length of the pencil?
mcqs.why: Add the two parts: 65 + 57 = 122 mm. Since 12 x 10 = 120 and 122 - 120 = 2, this is 12 cm 2 mm.

mcqs.q: In a walking race, Hamid walked 2 km 102 m and Hussain walked 1 km 985 m. How far ahead of Hussain was Hamid?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km: 2 km 102 m becomes 1 km 1102 m because 102 + 1000 = 1102. Then 1102 - 985 = 117, so Hamid was 117 m ahead of Hussain.

mcqs.q: In a 250 kilometre car race, a car had an accident 134 km from the winning point. What distance had the car driven before the accident?
mcqs.why: The car still had 134 km to go, so subtract from the full race: 250 - 134 = 116, meaning the car had driven 116 km before the accident.

mcqs.q: Naeem is 142 cm tall. His friend is 8 cm taller than Naeem. How tall is his friend?
mcqs.why: The friend is taller, so add: 142 + 8 = 150 cm. Since 1 x 100 = 100 and 150 - 100 = 50, this is 1 m 50 cm.

mcqs.q: A rope is 5 m 60 cm long. A piece of 1 m 75 cm is cut off. How much rope is left?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m: 5 m 60 cm becomes 4 m 160 cm because 60 + 100 = 160. Then 160 - 75 = 85 and 4 - 1 = 3, so 3 m 85 cm of rope is left.

mcqs.q: A boy walks 750 m in the morning and 650 m in the evening. What is the total distance he walks?
mcqs.why: Add the two walks: 750 + 650 = 1400 m. Since 1400 - 1000 = 400, this total is 1 km 400 m.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.4 — Convert Units of Time
lessons.notes_html:
Time units

  • 1 day = 24 hours
  • 1 hour = 60 minutes
  • 1 minute = 60 seconds

Big unit to small unit

Multiply by 60. Hours into minutes: 8 x 60 = 480, so 8 hours is 480 minutes. Minutes into seconds: 45 x 60 = 2700, so 45 minutes is 2700 seconds. For days, first change the days into hours: 2 x 24 = 48, so 2 days is 48 hours, and 48 x 60 = 2880, so 2 days is 2880 minutes.

Small unit to big unit

Divide by 60. The answer of the division gives the big unit and the remainder stays as the small unit. For seconds into hours, minutes and seconds, divide by 60 twice: first take out the minutes, then take the hours out of the minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 8 hours into minutes.
mcqs.why: Multiply hours by 60: 8 x 60 = 480, so 8 hours is 480 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 1 day 6 hours into minutes.
mcqs.why: 1 day is 24 hours, and 24 + 6 = 30 hours in total. Then 30 x 60 = 1800, so the time is 1800 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 45 minutes into seconds.
mcqs.why: Multiply minutes by 60: 45 x 60 = 2700, so 45 minutes is 2700 seconds.

mcqs.q: Convert 1 hour 25 minutes into seconds.
mcqs.why: 1 hour is 60 minutes, and 60 + 25 = 85 minutes. Then 85 x 60 = 5100, so the time is 5100 seconds.

mcqs.q: Convert 1180 minutes into hours and minutes.
mcqs.why: Divide by 60: 19 x 60 = 1140 and 1180 - 1140 = 40, so 1180 minutes is 19 hours and 40 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 2185 seconds into minutes and seconds.
mcqs.why: Divide by 60: 36 x 60 = 2160 and 2185 - 2160 = 25, so 2185 seconds is 36 minutes and 25 seconds.

mcqs.q: Convert 3800 seconds into hours, minutes and seconds.
mcqs.why: 1 hour is 3600 seconds, and 3800 - 3600 = 200 seconds left. Then 3 x 60 = 180 and 200 - 180 = 20, giving 1 h 3 min 20 s.

mcqs.q: Convert 2 days into minutes.
mcqs.why: 2 days is 48 hours because 2 x 24 = 48. Then 48 x 60 = 2880, so 2 days is 2880 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 2225 minutes into hours and minutes.
mcqs.why: Divide by 60: 37 x 60 = 2220 and 2225 - 2220 = 5, so 2225 minutes is 37 hours and 5 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 990 seconds into minutes and seconds.
mcqs.why: Divide by 60: 16 x 60 = 960 and 990 - 960 = 30, so 990 seconds is 16 minutes and 30 seconds.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.5 — Add and Subtract Time
lessons.notes_html:
Adding time

Add each unit in its own column: seconds with seconds, minutes with minutes, hours with hours. The limit here is 60, not 100.

  • 60 seconds or more: carry 1 minute, because 80 - 60 = 20 shows 80 seconds is 1 minute and 20 seconds.
  • 60 minutes or more: carry 1 hour.

Subtracting time

If the top seconds or minutes are too small, borrow from the unit above it.

  • Borrow 1 minute and it becomes 60 seconds.
  • Borrow 1 hour and it becomes 60 minutes.

Example: 20 + 60 = 80, so 62 min 20 s can be written as 61 min 80 s before subtracting.

mcqs.q: Add: 30 minutes 38 seconds and 20 minutes 42 seconds
mcqs.why: Seconds: 38 + 42 = 80 seconds, which is 1 min 20 s because 80 - 60 = 20. Minutes: 30 + 20 = 50, then 50 + 1 = 51, giving 51 min 20 s.

mcqs.q: Add: 4 hours 40 minutes and 3 hours 57 minutes
mcqs.why: Minutes: 40 + 57 = 97 minutes, which is 1 h 37 min because 97 - 60 = 37. Hours: 4 + 3 = 7, then 7 + 1 = 8, giving 8 h 37 min.

mcqs.q: Add: 3 hours 35 minutes 26 seconds and 2 hours 40 minutes 50 seconds
mcqs.why: Seconds: 26 + 50 = 76, which is 1 min 16 s because 76 - 60 = 16. Minutes become 35 + 40 = 75, then 75 + 1 = 76, which is 1 h 16 min. Hours: 3 + 2 = 5, then 5 + 1 = 6, giving 6 h 16 min 16 s.

mcqs.q: Subtract 38 minutes 39 seconds from 62 minutes 20 seconds.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 minute: 62 min 20 s becomes 61 min 80 s because 20 + 60 = 80. Then 80 - 39 = 41 and 61 - 38 = 23, giving 23 min 41 s.

mcqs.q: Subtract 44 minutes 25 seconds from 50 minutes.
mcqs.why: Write 50 minutes as 49 min 60 s because 49 + 1 = 50 and 1 minute is 60 seconds. Then 60 - 25 = 35 and 49 - 44 = 5, giving 5 min 35 s.

mcqs.q: Subtract 2 hours 58 minutes from 3 hours 5 minutes.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 hour: 3 h 5 min becomes 2 h 65 min because 5 + 60 = 65. Then 65 - 58 = 7 and 2 - 2 = 0 hours, so the answer is 7 min.

mcqs.q: Subtract 4 hours 32 minutes from 7 hours.
mcqs.why: Write 7 hours as 6 h 60 min. Then 60 - 32 = 28 and 6 - 4 = 2, giving 2 h 28 min.

mcqs.q: Subtract 3 hours 45 minutes 50 seconds from 5 hours 30 minutes 40 seconds.
mcqs.why: Borrow twice: the top becomes 4 h 89 min 100 s because 40 + 60 = 100 and 29 + 60 = 89. Then 100 - 50 = 50, 89 - 45 = 44 and 4 - 3 = 1, giving 1 h 44 min 50 s.

mcqs.q: Add: 47 minutes 25 seconds and 19 minutes 49 seconds
mcqs.why: Seconds: 25 + 49 = 74, which is 1 min 14 s because 74 - 60 = 14. Minutes become 47 + 19 = 66, then 66 + 1 = 67, which is 1 h 7 min because 67 - 60 = 7, giving 1 h 7 min 14 s.

mcqs.q: Add: 2 hours 55 minutes 45 seconds and 3 hours 48 minutes 44 seconds
mcqs.why: Seconds: 45 + 44 = 89, which is 1 min 29 s because 89 - 60 = 29. Minutes become 55 + 48 = 103, then 103 + 1 = 104, which is 1 h 44 min because 104 - 60 = 44. Hours: 2 + 3 = 5, then 5 + 1 = 6, giving 6 h 44 min 29 s.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.6 — Convert Days, Weeks, Months and Years
lessons.notes_html:
Calendar facts used in this book

  • 1 week = 7 days
  • 1 month = 30 days (the rule used in this book)
  • 1 year = 12 months

Method

To change a small unit into a bigger unit, divide and keep the remainder as the small unit.

  • Days into weeks and days: divide by 7. Example: 6 x 7 = 42 and 46 - 42 = 4, so 46 days is 6 weeks 4 days.
  • Days into months and days: divide by 30.
  • Months into years and months: divide by 12. Example: 5 x 12 = 60 and 66 - 60 = 6, so 66 months is 5 years 6 months.

To go the other way, from a big unit to a small unit, multiply: weeks by 7, months by 30, years by 12.

mcqs.q: Convert 46 days into weeks and days.
mcqs.why: Divide by 7: 6 x 7 = 42 and 46 - 42 = 4, so 46 days is 6 weeks and 4 days.

mcqs.q: Convert 213 days into weeks and days.
mcqs.why: Divide by 7: 30 x 7 = 210 and 213 - 210 = 3, so 213 days is 30 weeks and 3 days.

mcqs.q: Convert 450 days into months.
mcqs.why: The book uses 30 days in a month. Divide by 30: 15 x 30 = 450, so 450 days is exactly 15 months with nothing left over.

mcqs.q: Convert 800 days into months and days.
mcqs.why: Divide by 30: 26 x 30 = 780 and 800 - 780 = 20, so 800 days is 26 months and 20 days.

mcqs.q: Convert 66 months into years and months.
mcqs.why: Divide by 12: 5 x 12 = 60 and 66 - 60 = 6, so 66 months is 5 years and 6 months.

mcqs.q: Convert 82 months into years and months.
mcqs.why: Divide by 12: 6 x 12 = 72 and 82 - 72 = 10, so 82 months is 6 years and 10 months.

mcqs.q: Convert 49 months into years and months.
mcqs.why: Divide by 12: 4 x 12 = 48 and 49 - 48 = 1, so 49 months is 4 years and 1 month.

mcqs.q: Convert 2343 days into weeks and days.
mcqs.why: Divide by 7: 334 x 7 = 2338 and 2343 - 2338 = 5, so 2343 days is 334 weeks and 5 days.

mcqs.q: Convert 710 days into months and days.
mcqs.why: Divide by 30: 23 x 30 = 690 and 710 - 690 = 20, so 710 days is 23 months and 20 days.

mcqs.q: Convert 244 months into years and months.
mcqs.why: Divide by 12: 20 x 12 = 240 and 244 - 240 = 4, so 244 months is 20 years and 4 months.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.7 — Word Problems on Time
lessons.notes_html:
Method for time word problems

  • To compare two times, first change both into the same unit, usually minutes: 60 + 15 = 75 shows that 1 hour 15 minutes is 75 minutes.
  • Total time means add the times, and carry 1 hour when the minutes reach 60.
  • How much more or how much shorter means subtract the smaller time from the bigger time.
  • For days and months, this book uses 1 month = 30 days: 2 x 30 = 60 shows that 2 months is 60 days.

Always write the answer in a clear form, like hours and minutes, not as minutes greater than 60.

mcqs.q: Umair plays for 1 hour 15 minutes and Ali plays for 55 minutes. Who plays for the shorter period and by how much?
mcqs.why: Umair plays 75 minutes because 60 + 15 = 75. Then 75 - 55 = 20, so Ali plays for the shorter period, by 20 minutes.

mcqs.q: Fatima takes 1 hour 20 minutes for her Mathematics homework and 50 minutes for her English homework. How much total time does she take for both subjects?
mcqs.why: Add: 1 h 20 min plus 50 min gives 1 h 70 min. Since 70 - 60 = 10, this is 1 extra hour and 10 minutes, giving 2 h 10 min in total.

mcqs.q: School closes for summer vacations for 2 months and 5 days, while the other holidays are for 27 days. For how many days in total will the school remain closed?
mcqs.why: 2 months 5 days is 65 days because 2 x 30 = 60 and 60 + 5 = 65. Then 65 + 27 = 92, so the school remains closed for 92 days.

mcqs.q: At a library Hassan reads a newspaper for 36 minutes and then reads a magazine for 1 hour 50 minutes. How long does he spend in reading?
mcqs.why: Add 36 minutes to 1 h 50 min: the minutes become 36 + 50 = 86, which is 1 h 26 min because 86 - 60 = 26. Total hours: 1 + 1 = 2, giving 2 h 26 min.

mcqs.q: Adil takes 2 hours 9 minutes to complete a video game, while Ali takes 55 minutes for the same game. How much more time does Adil take than Ali?
mcqs.why: Adil takes 129 minutes because 2 x 60 = 120 and 120 + 9 = 129. Then 129 - 55 = 74 minutes, and 74 - 60 = 14, so Adil takes 1 h 14 min more.

mcqs.q: Sara plays for 1 hour 30 minutes and her brother plays for 45 minutes. What is the total playing time of both?
mcqs.why: 1 h 30 min is 90 minutes because 60 + 30 = 90. Then 90 + 45 = 135 minutes, and 135 - 120 = 15, so the total is 2 h 15 min.

mcqs.q: A bus journey takes 2 hours 45 minutes and a train journey takes 1 hour 50 minutes. How much longer is the bus journey?
mcqs.why: Bus time is 165 minutes because 2 x 60 = 120 and 120 + 45 = 165. Train time is 110 minutes because 60 + 50 = 110. Then 165 - 110 = 55, so the bus journey is 55 minutes longer.

mcqs.q: A school holiday lasts 1 month and 10 days. How many days is this, using the book rule for a month?
mcqs.why: The book uses 30 days in a month, so 1 month 10 days is 30 + 10 = 40 days in total.

mcqs.q: A student studies for 40 minutes in the morning and 1 hour 20 minutes in the evening. What is the total study time?
mcqs.why: 1 h 20 min is 80 minutes because 60 + 20 = 80. Then 40 + 80 = 120 minutes, and 120 / 60 = 2, so the total study time is 2 hours.

mcqs.q: Bilal finishes a game in 1 hour 40 minutes. Omar finishes the same game in 70 minutes. How much more time does Bilal take?
mcqs.why: Bilal takes 100 minutes because 60 + 40 = 100. Then 100 - 70 = 30, so Bilal takes 30 minutes more than Omar.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.8 — Temperature: Thermometer and Scale Conversion
lessons.notes_html:
Temperature and the thermometer

Temperature tells us how hot or cold something is. It is measured with a thermometer. Read the scale up to the mark where the mercury stops.

Two scales

  • The Celsius scale is written as °C.
  • The Fahrenheit scale is written as °F.

Fahrenheit into Celsius

Use °C = (°F − 32) x 5/9: first subtract 32, then multiply by 5 and divide by 9. Example in steps: 41 - 32 = 9, then 9 x 5 = 45, then 45 / 9 = 5, so 41°F is 5°C.

Celsius into Fahrenheit

Use °F = °C x 9/5 + 32: first multiply by 9 and divide by 5, then add 32. Example in steps: 30 x 9 = 270, then 270 / 5 = 54, then 54 + 32 = 86, so 30°C is 86°F.

mcqs.q: On a thermometer, the mercury stops at the 35 mark on the Celsius scale. What is the temperature?
mcqs.why: Read the scale up to the mark where the mercury stops. The mark is 35 on the Celsius scale, so the temperature is 35 degrees Celsius, as in the exercise.

mcqs.q: Change 41°F to the Celsius scale.
mcqs.why: Use the Celsius formula step by step: first 41 - 32 = 9, then 9 x 5 = 45, then 45 / 9 = 5, so 41 degrees F is 5 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Change 95°F to the Celsius scale.
mcqs.why: First 95 - 32 = 63, then 63 x 5 = 315, then 315 / 9 = 35, so 95 degrees F is 35 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Change 68°F to the Celsius scale.
mcqs.why: First 68 - 32 = 36, then 36 x 5 = 180, then 180 / 9 = 20, so 68 degrees F is 20 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Change 122°F to the Celsius scale.
mcqs.why: First 122 - 32 = 90, then 90 x 5 = 450, then 450 / 9 = 50, so 122 degrees F is 50 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Change 30°C to the Fahrenheit scale.
mcqs.why: Use the Fahrenheit formula step by step: first 30 x 9 = 270, then 270 / 5 = 54, then 54 + 32 = 86, so 30 degrees C is 86 degrees F.

mcqs.q: Change 45°C to the Fahrenheit scale.
mcqs.why: First 45 x 9 = 405, then 405 / 5 = 81, then 81 + 32 = 113, so 45 degrees C is 113 degrees F.

mcqs.q: Change 20°C to the Fahrenheit scale.
mcqs.why: First 20 x 9 = 180, then 180 / 5 = 36, then 36 + 32 = 68, so 20 degrees C is 68 degrees F.

mcqs.q: Change 80°C to the Fahrenheit scale.
mcqs.why: First 80 x 9 = 720, then 720 / 5 = 144, then 144 + 32 = 176, so 80 degrees C is 176 degrees F.

mcqs.q: Change 167°F to the Celsius scale.
mcqs.why: First 167 - 32 = 135, then 135 x 5 = 675, then 675 / 9 = 75, so 167 degrees F is 75 degrees C.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.9 — Word Problems on Temperature
lessons.notes_html:
Method for temperature word problems

  • First change both temperatures to the same scale. Never compare °C directly with °F.
  • Celsius into Fahrenheit: multiply by 9, divide by 5, then add 32. Example in steps: 35 x 9 = 315, then 315 / 5 = 63, then 63 + 32 = 95, so 35°C is 95°F.
  • Fahrenheit into Celsius: subtract 32, multiply by 5, then divide by 9.
  • For a difference, subtract the smaller temperature from the bigger temperature after both are on the same scale.
  • The city or day with the bigger number on the same scale is the hotter one.

mcqs.q: The maximum temperature on a day in Hyderabad was 35°C. What was the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: First 35 x 9 = 315, then 315 / 5 = 63, then 63 + 32 = 95, so the maximum temperature in Hyderabad was 95 degrees F.

mcqs.q: On one day the temperature in Jacobabad was 113°F, whereas the temperature in Hyderabad was 40°C. Which city had the higher temperature and by how much?
mcqs.why: Change 113 degrees F to Celsius: first 113 - 32 = 81, then 81 x 5 = 405, then 405 / 9 = 45. Hyderabad is 40 degrees C, and 45 - 40 = 5, so Jacobabad was hotter by 5 degrees C.

mcqs.q: Ali was suffering from fever. His temperature at noon was 102°F. Convert this temperature into degrees Celsius.
mcqs.why: First 102 - 32 = 70, then 70 x 5 = 350. Now 350 / 9 is about 38.9, so the fever temperature is about 38.9 degrees C.

mcqs.q: On one day the maximum temperature in Sukkur was 104°F, whereas in Karachi it was 35°C. What was the difference in the temperatures of the two cities in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: Karachi is 35 degrees C: first 35 x 9 = 315, then 315 / 5 = 63, then 63 + 32 = 95 degrees F. Then 104 - 95 = 9, so the difference is 9 degrees F.

mcqs.q: The maximum temperature on a day in Sehwan Sharif was 86°F. The minimum temperature on that day was 20°C. What was the difference between the two temperatures in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: Change the minimum to Fahrenheit: first 20 x 9 = 180, then 180 / 5 = 36, then 36 + 32 = 68 degrees F. Then 86 - 68 = 18, so the difference is 18 degrees F.

mcqs.q: The temperature of a room is 25°C. What is this temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: First 25 x 9 = 225, then 225 / 5 = 45, then 45 + 32 = 77, so a room temperature of 25 degrees C is 77 degrees F.

mcqs.q: The temperature on a cool morning is 59°F. What is this temperature in degrees Celsius?
mcqs.why: First 59 - 32 = 27, then 27 x 5 = 135, then 135 / 9 = 15, so 59 degrees F is 15 degrees C.

mcqs.q: City A has a temperature of 104°F and City B has a temperature of 38°C. Which city is hotter and by how much, in degrees Celsius?
mcqs.why: Change 104 degrees F to Celsius: first 104 - 32 = 72, then 72 x 5 = 360, then 360 / 9 = 40. Then 40 - 38 = 2, so City A is hotter by 2 degrees C.

mcqs.q: The temperature at night falls to 15°C. What is this temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: First 15 x 9 = 135, then 135 / 5 = 27, then 27 + 32 = 59, so 15 degrees C is 59 degrees F.

mcqs.q: Water boils at 100°C. What is this temperature in degrees Fahrenheit?
mcqs.why: First 100 x 9 = 900, then 900 / 5 = 180, then 180 + 32 = 212, so 100 degrees C is 212 degrees F.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 5
lessons.notes_html:
Review of the whole unit

  • Length: 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm = 10 mm. Multiply to go to a smaller unit and divide to go to a bigger unit.
  • Time: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds. Carry or borrow 60, not 100.
  • Calendar: 1 week = 7 days, 1 month = 30 days in this book, 1 year = 12 months.
  • Temperature: °C = (°F − 32) x 5/9 and °F = °C x 9/5 + 32.

Mixed conversions

Change each part separately, then add. Example in steps: 28 x 1000 = 28000 and 28000 + 648 = 28648, so 28 km 648 m is 28648 m. For clock times, count in parts: from 5:30 to 6:00 is 30 minutes and from 6:00 to 6:15 is 15 minutes, and 30 + 15 = 45, so the total is 45 minutes.

mcqs.q: Convert 28 km 648 m into metres.
Convert 48 m 97 cm into centimetres.
Convert 76 cm 9 mm into millimetres.
mcqs.why: First 76 x 10 = 760, then 760 + 9 = 769, so 76 cm 9 mm is 769 mm.

mcqs.q: Convert 6 m 75 cm 8 mm into millimetres.
mcqs.why: Metres into millimetres: 6 x 1000 = 6000. Centimetres into millimetres: 75 x 10 = 750. Then 6000 + 750 = 6750 and 6750 + 8 = 6758, so the total is 6758 mm.

mcqs.q: Add: 38 minutes 42 seconds and 25 minutes 55 seconds
mcqs.why: Seconds: 42 + 55 = 97, which is 1 min 37 s because 97 - 60 = 37. Minutes become 38 + 25 = 63, then 63 + 1 = 64, which is 1 h 4 min because 64 - 60 = 4, giving 1 h 4 min 37 s.

mcqs.q: Add: 20 hours 30 minutes and 16 hours 43 minutes
mcqs.why: Minutes: 30 + 43 = 73, which is 1 h 13 min because 73 - 60 = 13. Hours: 20 + 16 = 36, then 36 + 1 = 37, giving 37 h 13 min.

mcqs.q: Add: 4 m 70 cm 9 mm and 3 m 80 cm 5 mm
mcqs.why: Millimetres: 9 + 5 = 14, which is 1 cm 4 mm. Centimetres become 70 + 80 = 150, then 150 + 1 = 151, which is 1 m 51 cm because 151 - 100 = 51. Metres: 4 + 3 = 7, then 7 + 1 = 8, giving 8 m 51 cm 4 mm.

mcqs.q: Subtract 22 km 895 m from 67 km 472 m.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km: the top becomes 66 km 1472 m because 472 + 1000 = 1472. Then 1472 - 895 = 577 and 66 - 22 = 44, giving 44 km 577 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract 39 hours 49 minutes from 76 hours 32 minutes.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 hour: the top becomes 75 h 92 min because 32 + 60 = 92. Then 92 - 49 = 43 and 75 - 39 = 36, giving 36 h 43 min.

mcqs.q: How much time passes from 5:30 to 6:15?
mcqs.why: From 5:30 to 6:00 is 30 minutes because 60 - 30 = 30. From 6:00 to 6:15 is 15 minutes. Then 30 + 15 = 45, so the total time is 45 minutes.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1 — Unitary Method: Price of One or Many Things
lessons.notes_html:
What is the Unitary Method?

The unitary method means first finding the value of one unit. Once we know the value of one, we can find the value of any number.

Two Easy Rules

  • If the price of one thing is given, multiply by the number of things needed.
  • If the price of many things is given, divide the total price by the number of things to get the price of one.
  • Remember: one dozen means 12 things, and one year has 12 months.

Example

One pen costs Rs 30. For 6 pens we multiply the price of one pen by 6. If 12 books cost Rs 480, we divide the total price by 12 to get the price of one book.

mcqs.q: The price of a pen is Rs 30. What is the price of 6 such pens?
mcqs.why: The price of one pen is given, so multiply by the number of pens: 30 × 6 = 180, so 6 pens cost Rs 180.

mcqs.q: One litre of petrol costs Rs 105.70. What is the price of 5 litres of petrol?
mcqs.why: The price of one litre is given, so multiply by the number of litres: 105.70 × 5 = 528.50, so 5 litres cost Rs 528.50.

mcqs.q: The price of 1 kg of rice is Rs 110. What is the price of 7 kg of rice?
mcqs.why: The price of one kilogram is given, so multiply by the number of kilograms: 110 × 7 = 770, so 7 kg of rice cost Rs 770.

mcqs.q: The rent of a house for one month is Rs 5000. What is the rent for one year?
mcqs.why: One year has 12 months, so multiply the rent for one month by 12: 5000 × 12 = 60000, so the rent for one year is Rs 60,000.

mcqs.q: The price of a dozen bananas is Rs 66. What is the price of 1 banana?
mcqs.why: One dozen means 12 bananas. The price of many is given, so divide by 12: 66 ÷ 12 = 5.5, so one banana costs Rs 5.50.

mcqs.q: The price of 12 books is Rs 480. What is the price of one book?
mcqs.why: The price of many books is given, so divide the total price by the number of books: 480 ÷ 12 = 40, so one book costs Rs 40.

mcqs.q: The price of 8 chocolates is Rs 36. What is the price of one chocolate?
mcqs.why: The price of many chocolates is given, so divide the total price by the number of chocolates: 36 ÷ 8 = 4.5, so one chocolate costs Rs 4.50.

mcqs.q: The price of ten balls is Rs 205. What is the price of one ball?
mcqs.why: The price of many balls is given, so divide the total price by the number of balls: 205 ÷ 10 = 20.5, so one ball costs Rs 20.50.

mcqs.q: The price of three mobile phones is Rs 38400. What is the price of one mobile phone?
mcqs.why: The price of many phones is given, so divide the total price by the number of phones: 38400 ÷ 3 = 12800, so one phone costs Rs 12,800.

mcqs.q: The price of 16 pairs of socks is Rs 1004.80. What is the price of one pair of socks?
mcqs.why: The price of many pairs is given, so divide the total price by the number of pairs: 1004.80 ÷ 16 = 62.8, so one pair of socks costs Rs 62.80.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2 — Unitary Method: Many to Many
lessons.notes_html:
From Many to Many

Sometimes the price of many things is given and we need the price of a different number of things. Use the unitary method in two steps.

Steps

  • Step 1: Find the value of one unit by dividing.
  • Step 2: Multiply the value of one unit by the number needed.
  • In direct proportion, both quantities grow together or shrink together.
  • In inverse proportion, one quantity grows while the other becomes smaller, like more farmers taking less time to plough a field.

Example

If 6 balls cost Rs 240, first divide to find the price of one ball, then multiply by 10 to find the price of 10 balls.

mcqs.q: The price of 6 balls is Rs 240. Find the price of 10 such balls.
mcqs.why: First find the price of one ball: 240 ÷ 6 = 40, then scale up to 10 balls: 40 × 10 = 400, so 10 balls cost Rs 400.

mcqs.q: The cost of 10 books is Rs 240. What will be the cost of 15 such books?
mcqs.why: First find the cost of one book: 240 ÷ 10 = 24, then scale up to 15 books: 24 × 15 = 360, so 15 books cost Rs 360.

mcqs.q: The price of 2 dozen pencils is Rs 60. What is the price of 3 and a half dozen pencils?
mcqs.why: First find the price of one dozen: 60 ÷ 2 = 30, then scale up to three and a half dozen: 30 × 3.5 = 105, so the price is Rs 105.

mcqs.q: 6 farmers plough a field in 10 hours. How many hours will 8 farmers take to plough the same field?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, so the total work stays the same: 6 × 10 = 60 farmer-hours, then divide by the new number of farmers: 60 ÷ 8 = 7.5, so 8 farmers take 7.5 hours.

mcqs.q: The rent of a house for 3 months is Rs 18000. What is the rent for 8 months?
mcqs.why: First find the rent for one month: 18000 ÷ 3 = 6000, then scale up to 8 months: 6000 × 8 = 48000, so the rent for 8 months is Rs 48,000.

mcqs.q: A car travels 45 km in 3.5 litres of petrol. How far will it travel with 364 litres of petrol?
mcqs.why: First find how many times 3.5 litres fits into 364 litres: 364 ÷ 3.5 = 104, then scale the distance: 45 × 104 = 4680, so the car travels 4680 km. The book rounds the rate per litre, which does not multiply exactly; this grouping method gives the exact answer.

mcqs.q: 6 metres of cloth is required for 2 shirts. How many such shirts can be made from 42 metres of cloth?
mcqs.why: First find the cloth for one shirt: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 metres, then divide the cloth we have by the cloth per shirt: 42 ÷ 3 = 14, so 14 shirts can be made.

mcqs.q: 12 coaches carry 624 passengers. How many passengers will 18 such coaches carry?
mcqs.why: First find the passengers in one coach: 624 ÷ 12 = 52, then scale up to 18 coaches: 52 × 18 = 936, so 18 coaches carry 936 passengers.

mcqs.q: The weight of 16 bags of rice is 775.60 kg. What will be the weight of 24 such bags?
mcqs.why: First find the weight of one bag: 775.60 ÷ 16 = 48.475 kg, then scale up to 24 bags: 48.475 × 24 = 1163.4, so 24 bags weigh 1163.40 kg.

mcqs.q: The bus fare of 10 persons from Karachi to Larkana is Rs 8300. What is the fare for 36 persons?
mcqs.why: First find the fare for one person: 8300 ÷ 10 = 830, then scale up to 36 persons: 830 × 36 = 29880, so the fare for 36 persons is Rs 29,880.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3 — Ratio and Proportion
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Ratio?

A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind. We write it with a colon, like 3 : 5, which means the first quantity has 3 parts and the second has 5 parts. More parts means a greater quantity.

Rules for Ratios

  • Always change both quantities to the same unit before writing a ratio, like days and weeks both in days.
  • Make the ratio simple by dividing both numbers by the same number.
  • In direct proportion, both quantities increase together or decrease together.
  • In inverse proportion, one quantity increases while the other decreases, so their total product stays the same.

Example

For 3 boys to 6 girls, divide both numbers by 3 to get the simple ratio 1 : 2. More labourers doing more work is direct proportion, while more labourers needing fewer days is inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: The ratio of pocket money of Bismah and Omaima is 3 : 5. Who has more pocket money?
options: We cannot tell from the ratio
mcqs.why: In the ratio 3 : 5, Bismah has 3 parts and Omaima has 5 parts. More parts means more money, so Omaima has more pocket money than Bismah.

mcqs.q: The ratio of pocket money of Bismah and Omaima is 3 : 5. Is this statement true or false: Omaima has less pocket money than Bismah?
options: True, because Omaima has fewer parts
False, because Omaima has more parts
True, because Bismah is named first
False, because both girls have equal parts
mcqs.why: Bismah has 3 parts and Omaima has 5 parts, and 5 parts is greater than 3 parts, so Omaima has more money. The statement that she has less is false.

mcqs.q: Express 3 boys to 6 girls as a ratio in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: Divide both numbers by 3 to make the ratio simple: 3 ÷ 3 = 1 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2, so 3 boys to 6 girls gives the simplest ratio 1 : 2.

mcqs.q: Express 25 minutes to 80 minutes as a ratio in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: Both quantities are already in minutes. Divide both numbers by 5: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 and 80 ÷ 5 = 16, so the simplest ratio is 5 : 16.

mcqs.q: Express 5 days to 3 weeks as a ratio in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: First change weeks into days: 3 × 7 = 21 days, so we compare 5 days with 21 days. The numbers 5 and 21 share no common divisor, so the ratio stays 5 : 21.

mcqs.q: Express 250 kg to 1.5 kg as a ratio in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: Multiply both numbers by 2 to remove the decimal point: 250 × 2 = 500 and 1.5 × 2 = 3, so 250 kg to 1.5 kg gives the ratio 500 : 3.

mcqs.q: More labourers need fewer days to finish the same work. Is this direct or inverse proportion?
mcqs.why: When the number of labourers increases, the number of days decreases. One quantity grows while the other becomes smaller, so this is inverse proportion.

mcqs.q: If 2 packs of juice cost Rs 24, what is the cost of 4 packs of juice?
mcqs.why: First find the cost of one pack: 24 ÷ 2 = 12, then scale up to 4 packs: 12 × 4 = 48, so 4 packs of juice cost Rs 48.

mcqs.q: If 9 workers can complete a work in 6 days, how many workers are required to complete the same work in 3 days?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, so first find the total work: 9 × 6 = 54 worker-days, then divide by the new number of days: 54 ÷ 3 = 18, so 18 workers are required.

mcqs.q: 180 soldiers have food stock for 6 days. How many soldiers can eat the same food for 9 days?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, so first find the total food: 180 × 6 = 1080 soldier-days, then divide by the new number of days: 1080 ÷ 9 = 120, so 120 soldiers can eat for 9 days.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6
lessons.notes_html:
Review of the Unit

This unit brings together the unitary method, ratio and proportion. For every question, first decide whether to find the value of one unit or whether the total work stays the same.

Quick Checklist

  • Price of one given: multiply. Price of many given: divide to get one, then multiply for the number needed.
  • One dozen means 12, one hour means 60 minutes, and one year means 12 months.
  • More workers taking less time is inverse proportion: multiply to get the total work, then divide.
  • Keep the units the same on both sides before you compare or divide.

Example

If 6 packets of chalk cost Rs 90, divide to get the price of one packet, then multiply by 8 for the price of 8 packets.

mcqs.q: The cost of a sharpener is Rs 4.50. Find the cost of a dozen sharpeners.
mcqs.why: One dozen means 12 sharpeners. The cost of one is given, so multiply by 12: 4.50 × 12 = 54, so a dozen sharpeners cost Rs 54.

mcqs.q: From Karachi to Nawabshah, the bus fare of 10 persons is Rs 6500. What is the fare of each person?
mcqs.why: The fare of many persons is given, so divide the total fare by the number of persons: 6500 ÷ 10 = 650, so the fare of each person is Rs 650.

mcqs.q: The cost of 2 dozen eggs is Rs 220. What is the cost of 3 dozen eggs?
mcqs.why: First find the cost of one dozen: 220 ÷ 2 = 110, then scale up to 3 dozen: 110 × 3 = 330, so 3 dozen eggs cost Rs 330.

mcqs.q: If 10 persons can do a work in 6 days, in how many days can 15 persons do the same work?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, so first find the total work: 10 × 6 = 60 person-days, then divide by the new number of persons: 60 ÷ 15 = 4, so 15 persons take 4 days.

mcqs.q: The price of 6 packets of chalk is Rs 90. What is the price of 8 packets of chalk?
mcqs.why: First find the price of one packet: 90 ÷ 6 = 15, then scale up to 8 packets: 15 × 8 = 120, so 8 packets of chalk cost Rs 120.

mcqs.q: A printer prints 7620 papers in 1 hour. How many papers will it print in 40 minutes?
mcqs.why: One hour has 60 minutes. First find the papers printed in one minute: 7620 ÷ 60 = 127, then scale up to 40 minutes: 127 × 40 = 5080, so the printer prints 5080 papers.

mcqs.q: A train travels 800 km in 6 hours. How much distance will it travel in 15 hours at the same speed?
mcqs.why: Use the exact total method: 800 × 15 = 12000 and 12000 ÷ 6 = 2000, so the train travels 2000 km. The book writes the speed as a rounded decimal and multiplies it, which does not give exactly 2000; the method here avoids that rounding error and gives the correct answer.

mcqs.q: The price of 5 pens is Rs 150. What is the price of 9 such pens?
mcqs.why: First find the price of one pen: 150 ÷ 5 = 30, then scale up to 9 pens: 30 × 9 = 270, so 9 pens cost Rs 270.

mcqs.q: 12 workers can build a wall in 8 days. How many days will 16 workers take to build the same wall?
mcqs.why: This is inverse proportion, so first find the total work: 12 × 8 = 96 worker-days, then divide by the new number of workers: 96 ÷ 16 = 6, so 16 workers take 6 days.

mcqs.q: The cost of 4 notebooks is Rs 200. What is the cost of 7 such notebooks?
mcqs.why: First find the cost of one notebook: 200 ÷ 4 = 50, then scale up to 7 notebooks: 50 × 7 = 350, so 7 notebooks cost Rs 350.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1 — Names and Measures of Angles
lessons.notes_html:
What is an angle?

An angle is formed when two rays meet at a common point called the vertex. The two rays are called the arms of the angle. Angles are measured in degrees with a protractor.

Types of angles by measure

  • Acute angle: less than 90 degrees.
  • Right angle: exactly 90 degrees. Its arms are perpendicular to each other.
  • Obtuse angle: greater than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees.
  • Straight angle: exactly 180 degrees. It looks like a straight line.
  • Reflex angle: greater than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees.

Measuring an angle

Place the centre of the protractor on the vertex and the zero line on one arm. Read the mark where the second arm crosses the scale. That number is the measure of the angle.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 50 degrees?
mcqs.why: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees, and 50 is less than 90, so a 50 degrees angle is acute.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures exactly 90 degrees?
mcqs.why: A right angle is exactly 90 degrees by definition, like the corner of a book or a square.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 120 degrees?
mcqs.why: An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees, and 120 lies between 90 and 180.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 280 degrees?
mcqs.why: A reflex angle is greater than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees, and 280 lies between 180 and 360.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures exactly 180 degrees?
mcqs.why: A straight angle is exactly 180 degrees and its two arms point in opposite directions forming a straight line.

mcqs.q: An angle measured with a protractor is about 30 degrees and its arms are not perpendicular. What is it?
mcqs.why: 30 is less than 90, so the angle is acute. In the exercise the 30 degrees angle is the acute one.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 85 degrees?
mcqs.why: 85 is less than 90, so an 85 degrees angle is acute, just 5 degrees smaller than a right angle.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 200 degrees?
mcqs.why: 200 is greater than 180 and less than 360, so a 200 degrees angle is a reflex angle.

mcqs.q: What type of angle measures 150 degrees?
mcqs.why: 150 is greater than 90 and less than 180, so a 150 degrees angle is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: Two arms of an angle are perpendicular to each other. What is the measure of the angle?
mcqs.why: Perpendicular arms always meet at a right angle, and a right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2 — Measuring and Drawing Reflex Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Reflex angles

A reflex angle is greater than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees. It is the larger turn between two arms.

Measuring a reflex angle

  • Measure the smaller angle between the arms with a protractor.
  • Subtract it from 360 degrees: reflex angle = 360 degrees minus the smaller angle.

Drawing a reflex angle

  • First find the smaller angle: 360 degrees minus the reflex angle you want.
  • Draw that smaller angle with a protractor.
  • Mark the arc on the outside of the smaller angle. The outside part is the reflex angle.

To draw a straight angle, draw a straight line, which is 180 degrees. To draw a right angle, use 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: The smaller angle between two arms is 25 degrees. What is the reflex angle?
mcqs.why: Reflex angle = 360 - 25 = 335, so the reflex angle is 335 degrees, as in the exercise.

mcqs.q: The smaller angle is 30 degrees. What is the reflex angle?
mcqs.why: Reflex angle = 360 - 30 = 330, so the reflex angle between the arms is 330 degrees.

mcqs.q: The smaller angle is 90 degrees. What is the reflex angle?
mcqs.why: Reflex angle = 360 - 90 = 270, so when the smaller angle is a right angle the reflex angle is 270 degrees.

mcqs.q: The smaller angle is 80 degrees. What is the reflex angle?
mcqs.why: Reflex angle = 360 - 80 = 280, so the reflex angle is 280 degrees, as in the exercise.

mcqs.q: To draw a reflex angle of 310 degrees, what smaller angle should you draw first?
mcqs.why: Smaller angle = 360 - 310 = 50, so draw a 50 degrees angle and mark the arc outside it.

mcqs.q: To draw a reflex angle of 280 degrees, what smaller angle should you draw first?
mcqs.why: Smaller angle = 360 - 280 = 80, so draw an 80 degrees angle first and take the outside part.

mcqs.q: To draw a reflex angle of 340 degrees, what smaller angle should you draw first?
mcqs.why: Smaller angle = 360 - 340 = 20, so draw a small 20 degrees angle and mark the big outside arc.

mcqs.q: To draw a reflex angle of 290 degrees, what smaller angle should you draw first?
mcqs.why: Smaller angle = 360 - 290 = 70, so draw a 70 degrees angle first to get the 290 degrees reflex angle.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a reflex angle?
mcqs.why: A reflex angle is greater than 180 degrees and less than 360 degrees. Only 250 degrees fits this rule.

mcqs.q: Angle PQR is a right angle. What is its measure?
mcqs.why: A right angle always measures exactly 90 degrees, so angle PQR measures 90 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.3 — Adjacent, Complementary and Supplementary Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Adjacent angles

Two angles are adjacent when they have a common vertex, a common arm, and they do not overlap each other. If one angle lies inside the other, they are not adjacent. If their vertices are different, they cannot be adjacent.

Complementary angles

Two angles are complementary when their measures add up to 90 degrees. Complement of an angle = 90 degrees minus the angle.

Supplementary angles

Two angles are supplementary when their measures add up to 180 degrees. Supplement of an angle = 180 degrees minus the angle.

Remember: complementary and supplementary describe the sum of measures, while adjacent describes the position of the angles. A pair can be both, only one, or neither.

mcqs.q: What is the complement of 60 degrees?
mcqs.why: Complement = 90 - 60 = 30, so the complement of 60 degrees is 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the complement of 76 degrees?
mcqs.why: Complement = 90 - 76 = 14, so the complement of 76 degrees is 14 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the complement of 38 degrees?
mcqs.why: Complement = 90 - 38 = 52, so the complement of 38 degrees is 52 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the supplement of 25 degrees?
mcqs.why: Supplement = 180 - 25 = 155, so the supplement of 25 degrees is 155 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the supplement of 98 degrees?
mcqs.why: Supplement = 180 - 98 = 82, so the supplement of 98 degrees is 82 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the supplement of 143 degrees?
mcqs.why: Supplement = 180 - 143 = 37, so the supplement of 143 degrees is 37 degrees.

mcqs.q: The pair 49 degrees and 41 degrees is:
mcqs.why: Check the sum: 49 + 41 = 90, and a pair adding to 90 degrees is complementary.

mcqs.q: The pair 154 degrees and 26 degrees is:
mcqs.why: Check the sum: 154 + 26 = 180, and a pair adding to 180 degrees is supplementary.

mcqs.q: Which angle is equal to its own complement?
mcqs.why: Let the angle be x. Then x + x = 90, so 2 x = 90 and x = 90 / 2 = 45. The angle is 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: Can two obtuse angles be supplementary?
mcqs.why: Each obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees, so two of them add to more than 180 degrees and cannot be supplementary.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.4 — Types of Triangles
lessons.notes_html:
Triangles by sides

  • Equilateral triangle: all three sides are equal.
  • Isosceles triangle: two sides are equal.
  • Scalene triangle: all three sides are different.

Triangles by angles

  • Acute-angled triangle: all three angles are less than 90 degrees.
  • Right-angled triangle: one angle is exactly 90 degrees.
  • Obtuse-angled triangle: one angle is greater than 90 degrees.

Measure the sides with a ruler and the angles with a protractor, then name the triangle. The three angles of every triangle add up to 180 degrees.

mcqs.q: A triangle has all three sides equal. What is it called?
mcqs.why: A triangle with all three sides equal is called an equilateral triangle, like the 4 cm, 4 cm, 4 cm triangle in the exercise.

mcqs.q: A triangle has exactly two sides equal. What is it called?
mcqs.why: A triangle with two equal sides is called an isosceles triangle. The third side is different from the equal pair.

mcqs.q: A triangle has all three sides different. What is it called?
mcqs.why: A triangle with all sides different is called a scalene triangle. No two of its sides have the same length.

mcqs.q: A triangle has one angle greater than 90 degrees. What is it called?
mcqs.why: A triangle with one angle greater than 90 degrees is called an obtuse-angled triangle.

mcqs.q: A triangle has one angle exactly 90 degrees. What is it called?
mcqs.why: A triangle with one angle of exactly 90 degrees is called a right-angled triangle.

mcqs.q: A triangle has all three angles less than 90 degrees. What is it called?
mcqs.why: When all three angles are acute, that is less than 90 degrees each, the triangle is acute-angled.

mcqs.q: The sides of a triangle are 5 cm, 5 cm and 5 cm. Its name by sides is:
mcqs.why: All three sides are 5 cm, so they are all equal, and the triangle is equilateral.

mcqs.q: The sides of a triangle are 4 cm, 6 cm and 5 cm. Its name by sides is:
mcqs.why: The sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 5 cm are all different from each other, so the triangle is scalene.

mcqs.q: The sides of a triangle are 6 cm, 6 cm and 4 cm. Its name by sides is:
mcqs.why: Two sides are 6 cm and 6 cm, so exactly two sides are equal and the triangle is isosceles.

mcqs.q: Which tool is used to measure the angles of a triangle?
mcqs.why: Angles are measured in degrees with a protractor. A ruler measures lengths of sides, not angles.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.5 — Construction of Triangles
lessons.notes_html:
Construction with three sides (SSS)

  • Draw the base side with a ruler.
  • Open the compasses to the second side length and draw an arc from one end of the base.
  • Open the compasses to the third side length and draw an arc from the other end so the arcs meet.
  • Join the meeting point to both ends of the base. This point is the third vertex.

Construction with a side and two angles (ASA)

Draw the side, make the given angles at its two ends with a protractor, and extend the arms until they meet. The third angle = 180 degrees minus the sum of the two given angles.

Construction with an angle and its two sides (SAS)

Draw the first side, make the given angle at one end, cut the second side on the new arm, then join the points.

Hypotenuse

In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite the right angle is called the hypotenuse. It is the longest side of the triangle.

mcqs.q: To construct an equilateral triangle of side 4 cm, what arcs are drawn from the ends of the 4 cm base?
mcqs.why: In an equilateral triangle all sides are 4 cm, so both arcs are drawn with compasses opened to 4 cm.

mcqs.q: For isosceles triangle ABC with AB = BC = 6 cm and base AC = 4 cm, the arcs from A and C are:
mcqs.why: The sides from A and C up to B are AB = 6 cm and CB = 6 cm, so both arcs are 6 cm arcs.

mcqs.q: For scalene triangle ABC with AB = 4.8 cm, BC = 3 cm and AC = 5 cm, using AB as base, the arcs from A and B are:
options: 5 cm from A and 3 cm from B
3 cm from A and 5 cm from B
mcqs.why: The side from A is AC = 5 cm and the side from B is BC = 3 cm, so the arcs are 5 cm from A and 3 cm from B.

mcqs.q: A triangle has two angles 60 degrees and 60 degrees. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: Third angle = 180 - 60 - 60 = 60, so all three angles are 60 degrees and the triangle is equilateral.

mcqs.q: A triangle has two angles 70 degrees and 70 degrees. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: Third angle = 180 - 70 - 70 = 40, so the third angle of the isosceles triangle is 40 degrees.

mcqs.q: A triangle has two angles 60 degrees and 50 degrees. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: Third angle = 180 - 60 - 50 = 70, so the third angle of this scalene triangle is 70 degrees.

mcqs.q: In triangle ABC the right angle is at C. Which side is the hypotenuse?
mcqs.why: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle. The right angle is at C, so the side opposite it is AB.

mcqs.q: In triangle PQR the right angle is at Q. Which side is the hypotenuse?
mcqs.why: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle at Q, so it is the side PR joining the other two vertices.

mcqs.q: A triangle has two angles 55 degrees and 35 degrees. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: Third angle = 180 - 55 - 35 = 90, so the third angle is 90 degrees and the triangle is right-angled.

mcqs.q: A triangle has two angles 75 degrees and 65 degrees. What is the third angle?
mcqs.why: Third angle = 180 - 75 - 65 = 40, so the third angle of the triangle is 40 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.7 — Quadrilaterals
lessons.notes_html:
Quadrilaterals

A quadrilateral is a closed shape with 4 sides, 4 angles and 4 vertices. The sum of its four angles is 360 degrees.

Some special quadrilaterals

  • Rhombus: all sides equal and opposite sides parallel.
  • Kite: two pairs of adjacent sides equal.
  • Trapezium: only one pair of opposite sides parallel.
  • Rectangle: opposite sides equal and every angle is 90 degrees.
  • Square: all sides equal and every angle is 90 degrees.

Constructing a rectangle or square

  • Draw the length side with a ruler.
  • Make 90 degrees angles at both ends with a protractor or set squares.
  • Cut the breadth measure on both arms.
  • Join the top ends to complete the shape. For a square, all four sides are equal.

mcqs.q: How many sides does a quadrilateral have?
mcqs.why: Every quadrilateral has exactly 4 sides, 4 angles and 4 vertices, as counted in the exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of all the angles of a quadrilateral?
mcqs.why: The four angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees. For example a rectangle: 90 + 90 + 90 + 90 = 360.

mcqs.q: A quadrilateral has all sides equal and opposite sides parallel. What is it?
mcqs.why: All sides equal with opposite sides parallel is the property of a rhombus, as identified in the exercise.

mcqs.q: A quadrilateral has two pairs of adjacent equal sides. What is it?
mcqs.why: A kite has two pairs of adjacent sides equal: the two shorter sides together and the two longer sides together.

mcqs.q: A quadrilateral has only one pair of parallel sides. What is it?
mcqs.why: Only one pair of opposite sides parallel is the special property of a trapezium.

mcqs.q: To construct a rectangle 4 cm by 3 cm, what angles are made at the ends of the 4 cm side?
mcqs.why: Every angle of a rectangle is 90 degrees, so 90 degrees angles are made at both ends of the length side.

mcqs.q: A square has side 5.4 cm. What is the length of each of its other sides?
mcqs.why: All four sides of a square are equal, so if one side is 5.4 cm, every other side is also 5.4 cm.

mcqs.q: How many vertices does a quadrilateral have?
mcqs.why: A quadrilateral has 4 corners, and each corner is a vertex, so it has exactly 4 vertices.

mcqs.q: Which of these can be used to make the 90 degrees corners of a rectangle?
mcqs.why: The exercise constructs rectangles with a ruler and protractor, and also with a ruler and set squares; both give 90 degrees corners.

mcqs.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90 degrees, 90 degrees and 90 degrees. What is the fourth angle?
mcqs.why: Fourth angle = 360 - 90 - 90 - 90 = 90, so the fourth angle is also 90 degrees, like in a rectangle.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7
lessons.notes_html:
Angles between directions

  • East and South make a right angle of 90 degrees.
  • East and West are opposite directions and make a straight angle of 180 degrees.
  • East and North make a right angle of 90 degrees.
  • From North to West through East is a reflex angle: 90 degrees plus 90 degrees plus 90 degrees equals 270 degrees.

Angles of a triangle

The three angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees. So a triangle cannot have two right angles or two obtuse angles, because those two alone reach or pass 180 degrees. A triangle also cannot have all angles less than 60 degrees, because the sum would stay less than 180 degrees.

Square and rectangle
